sect('## The target model\n', """
The layout every problem below is measured against:

```
flightdeck/launch/
  <name>/
    specs/
      interview/
      spec.v1.json
      test-map.v1.json
    runs/
      run-1/
      run-2/
  FLIGHTLOG.md
```

A **launch** is the folder for one piece of work. It is named for the feature it builds and it holds two things: the spec series that defines the work, and every run made against that series. A launch is opened once and stays open until a run is accepted. Under the flightcrew v1 system the word launch meant a single attempt; where this document quotes that system, it says so.

A **run** is one attempt at a launch. Runs are numbered in the order they are made and are disposable: a run that fails is ended, diagnosed, and never reopened. The next run starts clean against the same or an amended spec version. A launch accumulates runs until one succeeds.

The **spec series** lives under the launch in `specs/`, beside the runs it drives. Each version is an immutable file. A revision is a new file with the version incremented, never an edit. The `interview/` folder holds the material the spec was grown from: the idea, the questions, the findings, the judge and attacker verdicts. It is never copied anywhere.

**Run outputs** are what a run writes into its own folder: the kickoff version it was given, the plan, the event log, the check outputs, the review findings and the report. Run outputs belong to the run that made them.

**Setup** is what survives runs: the spec series, the tests map, the interview, the kickoff library, the agent definitions and the log. **Output** is what a run produces and a later run does not inherit.

The log is `FLIGHTLOG.md`, one file beside all launches, with one entry per run.
""")

sect('### 1. The system names an attempt where the work is a launch\n', """
**What.** The flightcrew v1 runner creates one folder per attempt and calls it a launch. `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/launch.mjs:267` refuses to open a folder that already exists, `launch exists: <path>`, and the flags it accepts at `launch.mjs:257` offer no override. Its default name, `launch.mjs:231-237`, is the spec name followed by the first free integer. The two completed attempts at building flightcrew were given the names `flightcrew-buildout` and `flightcrew-buildout-2` with the `--name` flag. The log `flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md` heads each entry with the date, the spec name and the folder name, so the entry for the second attempt reads as a run of a different thing rather than the second run of the same thing.

**Why it matters.** Under the target model the folder the runner creates is a run, and the thing it refuses to reuse is correct at that level: a run is never reopened. What is missing is the level above it. Nothing in the system names the launch, so the attempts of one piece of work have no common parent, no shared address, and no count. The refusal that protects a run from being resumed also prevents the work from ever having a home.

**Effect on the system.** Every consumer that should operate on a launch operates on a folder instead. The planner reads the log for prior runs of the same spec by matching the spec name in headings. The next attempt is found by scanning sibling folders. Two attempts at the same feature look identical to two unrelated features that happen to share a spec. The single word the system uses for both concepts hides the distinction from every agent that reads its output.
""")

sect('### 2. The spec is copied where it should be pointed at\n', """
**What.** `fc launch new` copies the spec file into the new folder at `launch.mjs:304-305`, and `fc launch pin tests-map` copies the map the same way. On this branch `flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/spec.v1.json`, `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/specs/flightcrew-v1/spec.v1.json` and `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/specs/flightcrew-v1/spec.v1.json` are the same git blob. Each copy is then added to the run's locked paths, `launch.mjs:443-444`, and the design contract at `flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/design.md:286` records the arrangement as intended: launches hold pinned copies.

The source guides this system was built from never copy the spec. The kickoff guide names the spec by path and frozen commit and says pointers, not copies, so there is exactly one version of the truth. The planning guide's plan header carries the spec as a path at a commit. The spec guide has the run log reference the commit the spec was frozen at.

**Why it matters.** `launch.json` already pins the spec by version and by the commit of the file, so the copy adds nothing the pin does not carry. What it adds is a second and third location where the bytes of the spec exist, each locked separately, each able to drift from the source without any check noticing. A single source of truth is the property the whole method rests on: the orchestrator, the test-builder and the critic must read the same definition of the work. Three files that happen to be identical today are not one file.

**Effect on the system.** Every launch folder is larger than its evidence by the size of the spec and map. The locked-path list of every map includes globs for the copies, so the lock guard and the changed-since-lock check spend effort defending files that should not exist. Under the target model, where the spec series lives inside the launch beside its runs, the copies become copies of a file in the parent folder. The design contract's statement that launches hold pinned copies is the line a planner has to reverse.
""")

sect('### 3. The spec-making stage has a home in the model and no owner in the system\n', """
**What.** The target model gives the interval before a spec is frozen an address: `specs/interview/` under the launch. Nothing in the flightcrew v1 system produces anything at that address. No command under `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/` creates a spec folder, an interview folder or an idea file. The only mention of `interview` in code is `flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/validators/validate-all.mjs:26`, where the validator lists it among directories to skip. The crew README at `flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/README.md:5` and `:28-41` describes a spec-stage dispatcher that passes fixed paths to the spec-builder, including the interview subdirectory. No such dispatcher exists among the twenty command modules. No interviewer role exists on any branch. The file `flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/spec-interviewer.md` is a zero-byte untracked file in the working tree, and `flightdeck/STRUCTURE.md` on branches `main` and `constitution-research` describes it as deliberately empty and the thing the next launch builds.

Every spec in the repository was nonetheless grown by exactly this process, by hand. On branch `constitution-research`, `flightdeck/launch/reference-library/` holds `idea.txt`, `interview/problems.json`, `interview/findings.json`, `interview/bundles/P1.json` through `P5.json`, and `spec.v1.json`. On `engage-crew`, `flightdeck/launch/agent-spec-interviewer/` holds the same shape plus `judge/` and `attacker/` verdicts. The runner accepts the result of that process only once it is a file: `launch.mjs:258-264` requires the spec path to exist and carry a name, and tolerates a draft, deferring the frozen check to `fc launch activate` at `launch.mjs:334-341`.

**Why it matters.** The source guides make the spec-building session stage one of the method, the cheapest exit in the whole process, and the place the human is the main character. It has three roles: an interviewer that asks and never drafts, an attacker in a fresh context, and a judge that rules on readiness. Two of the three exist as crew files on this branch. The stage they belong to has no command, no folder the tooling knows, and no recorded starting point. The interval in which the spec is made is the only interval the system does not model.

**Effect on the system.** Both runs that carry an interview shape have it because the operator knew the shape. Nothing in the repository states it, creates it or would reproduce it. A new launch begins wherever the human puts the first file, and the tooling meets the work only when a frozen spec is handed to it. Under the target model the address exists and is empty, which is an improvement on having no address, and is not yet a stage.
""")

sect('### 4. A run branch is recorded and never made\n', """
**What.** `launch.mjs:288` records a branch name in `launch.json`, defaulting to `run/<name>`, and never creates it. The only later use is at `launch.mjs:571-573`, where a mismatch between the checked-out branch and the recorded one produces a warning. `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/launch.json` records `run/flightcrew-buildout`. No such ref exists locally or on the remote. `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/launch.json` records `flightcrew-buildout-v1`, which is the trunk the buildout branch was later advanced from and which PR #1 merged into it. The first run's report, `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/report.md`, states that units ran as parallel build sessions in the repository working tree rather than in per-unit worktrees, so no unit branches were created.

The source guides do not agree on what becomes of a run's branch. The map page says that on exit the branch is left as it is. The endings guide's final abandonment step says delete the run's branches, remove its worktrees, prune.

**Why it matters.** The guides' isolation principle is one branch per run, cut at liftoff, with one worktree per worker and one atomic commit per unit, so that a failed unit is a discarded branch and a resumed run is a checkout. A recorded branch that was never cut gives the record the appearance of that discipline without the substance. A reader of `launch.json` learns a branch name that resolves to nothing, and a planner who believes the record will plan a resume that cannot happen.

**Effect on the system.** Neither run had a branch of its own, so neither run's work can be found by branch, and both runs' evidence is interleaved with the trunk's history. The branch convention `run/<name>` was abandoned on the second run rather than extended, and under the target model the convention itself needs a second component for the run number. The unresolved question in the guides, whether an abandoned run's branch is kept for its evidence or deleted to clear the ground, was inherited by the system and answered by making no branch at all.
""")

sect("### 5. The log cannot show lineage or hold the human's diagnosis\n", """
**What.** `flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/runlog-entry.template.md` defines two entry shapes. The abandoned and partial shape carries `seen on`, `cause`, `fixed on`, `change`, `watch`, `kept` and `promote`. The accepted shape carries `kept` and `reservation` and no axis field. `flightdeck/manuals/orchestration/run-log.md:60` states that the human writes the five diagnosis fields and commits the entry, and that an agent never writes a `<fill>` field. In `flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md:24-30` every diagnosis line of the first run's entry is prefixed `draft (orchestrator):`. The commit that added the entry, `733f79f`, describes the fields as filled by the human. A later commit, `19faef3`, relabelled them as orchestrator drafts. Both entries head with the date, the spec name and the folder name, `RUNLOG.md:3` and `:18`, so nothing in the heading says that the second entry is the second run of the first.

**Why it matters.** The log is the one document the target model preserves across runs by design, and the source guides call it the highest-leverage document in the project because the spec template, the kickoff library and the hook set are iterated against it. Its value depends on two properties. The diagnosis is the human's judgement about the setup, which the run could not see, and a machine's draft in its place turns the comparison between runs into fiction. The entries of one launch read as a sequence, so that a pattern pass can count axes per launch and the planner can read the prior runs of the work it is planning. The current log has neither property.

**Effect on the system.** The planner reads this file before writing a plan for the same spec, and finds the first run's failure and the second run's reservation presented as unrelated observations. The relationship survives only in a `previous_launch` field the log does not carry. Under the target model the log becomes `FLIGHTLOG.md` beside all launches, and its headings need the launch name and the run number so that lineage is visible without following pointers.
""")

sect('### 6. Documents describe shapes that were never built\n', """
**What.** `flightdeck/launch/README.md:7` describes the spec folder as holding `checks/` for check scripts with no natural project home and `interview/`, and `README.md:13-23` sketches a launch folder containing `hooks.log`. On this branch `flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/` holds `design.md`, `spec.v1.json`, `tests-map.v1.json` and `tests-map.v2.json`, no `checks/` and no `interview/`. Neither committed launch contains a `hooks.log`. `flightdeck/STRUCTURE.md`, which exists on `main` and `constitution-research` and not on this branch, shows `launch/example-launch/` containing `checks/` and `specs/`. An enumeration of every tree reachable from every ref finds no path containing `example-launch` and no `flightdeck/launch/<run>/checks/` anywhere in history. `flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/design.md:279` instructs that the existing empty `launch/flightcrew-buildout/checks/` and `specs/` folders are removed before the launch is created, which is why the directory appears in no commit. Both `launch.json` files record gate `G3` as pending while carrying a final outcome and the phase `ended`.

**Why it matters.** These documents are what an agent reads to learn the shape of the system. The source guides' context principle is that boundaries and decided questions are written down before the run starts, and that a role reads its own tailored context. A map that states intent as fact, a README that names files nothing produces, and a record that ends a run without its last gate each hand an agent a false premise that the agent has no way to test. The structure document even states its own standard, that it records directories only so it stays true as files churn, and then shows directories that never existed.

**Effect on the system.** A planner working from the README plans for a checks folder that no command creates and a hooks log that no hook writes. The check-building path already inherits the error: `flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/test-builder.md:22` names the spec folder's `checks/` as its final fallback for placing a check. The design contract's one-off removal instruction outlived the run it was written for and became the reason the artefact and the map disagree. Under the target model all three documents need rewriting, and until they are the layout decision changes nothing an agent can read.
""")

sect('### 7. Run outputs are not a defined set\n', """
**What.** The two completed launches hold different things. `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/` holds `returns/` with seven unit returns and a `notes.md`, and no files under `review/`. `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/` holds `review/` with two critic passes, no files under `returns/`, and no `notes.md`. `fc launch new` creates `evidence/`, `returns/` and `review/` as empty directories and an empty `events.jsonl`, `launch.mjs:304-309`, and git does not track the empty ones. The first run's `events.jsonl` carries nine `SubagentStart` events marked `source: stated`, each with the reason that the hooks were not installed and the start is recorded by hand. The second run's report records zero agents. Neither run's report header carries a token count; both read `not recorded`.

**Why it matters.** The target model treats run outputs as belonging to the run and as the material the log entry is written from. That only works if the set is known. The source guides make the report's provenance its most important property and judge a harness by the ratio of recorded lines to stated lines. A run whose agent starts are stated by hand, whose cost is not recorded, and whose folder holds whichever outputs the operator happened to produce is a run whose report cannot be compared with the next one.

**Effect on the system.** The report assembler renders what it finds, so the two reports differ in shape as well as content. The endings guide expects an abandoned run's report to be assembled anyway and kept, because the log entry is written from it, and the target model has not yet said whether an abandoned run's outputs are kept, archived or overwritten. Until the set of run outputs is fixed and each item's fate is decided, the run folder is a directory of leftovers rather than a record.
""")

sect('### 8. Three shapes exist across branches\n', """
**What.** Three incompatible layouts for a spec and its runs exist in this repository at once. On `flightcrew-buildout`, the spec series sits in `flightdeck/launch/specs/<name>/` outside every run folder. On `engage-crew`, twelve agent-type specs sit grouped under `flightdeck/launch/agent-types/specs/`. On `constitution-research` and `engage-crew`, the spec sits inside the run folder beside `interview/`, `judge/` and `attacker/`, as in `flightdeck/launch/reference-library/` and `flightdeck/launch/agent-spec-interviewer/`. The third shape is the one every spec in the repository was produced under. The first is the one the tooling enforces.

**Why it matters.** The target model is a fourth shape. It is closest to the third, in that the spec and its interview sit with the work, and it adds the runs as numbered children. Adopting it settles the question for new launches and settles nothing for the folders that exist. The branches that hold the third shape are user-facing discovery work that the user has asked to keep.

**Effect on the system.** A tool written to the target model will find folders on other branches that it cannot read, and a validator that walks `flightdeck/launch/` will meet three layouts. The migration of the existing folders to the new shape is a separate piece of work from the layout decision, and this document records it as one of the decisions the model forces rather than as part of the model.
""")

sect('## Dissolved by the model\n', """
An earlier diagnosis of these problems, written before the source guides were read, treated the second attempt at building flightcrew as a defect of identity: one piece of work occupying two folders, a run with no concept of an attempt, a pointer standing in for containment, and a version series hoisted out of the run because the run could not hold it. Under the target model, and under the guides it comes from, none of those is a defect.

- **Two folders for two attempts.** A run is disposable and is never resumed with corrections. Two attempts are two runs, and the guides' own layout numbers them as siblings under one parent. The defect is the missing parent, recorded as problem 1, not the sibling folders.
- **No attempt field in the run record.** A run is one attempt by definition. The field that is missing is the launch it belongs to, not an attempt counter inside it.
- **The refusal to reuse a run folder.** Correct at the level of a run. The guides forbid reopening an abandoned session and forbid the changeless retry.
- **The version series outside the run.** The spec series is setup and survives every run. It belongs outside every run folder. The guides place it in a per-spec folder; the target model places it in the launch folder beside the runs. Both keep it out of the run.
- **Two log entries for one spec.** One entry per run is the guides' rule. The defect is that the entries do not show they belong to one launch, recorded as problem 5.
""")

sect('## Decisions the model forces\n', """
- Whether an abandoned run's branch is kept for its evidence or deleted to clear the ground. The two source guides disagree and the system inherited the disagreement.
- Whether an abandoned run's outputs, and its report in particular, are kept in place, archived, or overwritten once its log entry is written.
- Whether the two completed launches on `flightcrew-buildout` are left as they are or moved. Moving them requires editing two frozen tests maps whose locked paths name the old spec folder, both `launch.json` files whose paths point inside their own folders, a runner that hardcodes the old spec path when it locks, and a locked suite that asserts the log's filename.
- Whether the spec folders on `constitution-research` and `engage-crew`, which hold the third shape, are migrated to the target model, left in place, or both.
""")

open(p,'w').write(head+'# Structure problems\n'+body)
EOF
grep -c '' structure-problems.md; grep -n '^#' structure-problems.md
Description: Write the prose under each heading, leaving comments in place

------------------------------------------------------------

[BASH TOOL]
Command: python3 - <<'EOF'
p='structure-problems.md'
body=open(p).read()

def sect(marker, prose):
    global body
    i=body.index(marker); j=i+len(marker)
    lines=body[j:].split('\n'); k=0
    while k<len(lines) and (lines[k].startswith('<!--') or lines[k]==''):
        if lines[k]=='' and k+1<len(lines) and lines[k+1].startswith('#'): break
        k+=1
    body=body[:j]+'\n'.join(lines[:k])+'\n'+prose.strip('\n')+'\n'+'\n'.join(lines[k:])

P={}
P['# Structure problems\n']="""
This document describes the structure problems of the flightcrew orchestration system: how a piece of work, its spec, its attempts and its record are named and laid out on disk. It is one of a set of problem documents, each covering one domain, written to inform the plan of a later launch that will address them. It diagnoses. It proposes no remediation.

Every observation was verified on branch `flightcrew-buildout` at commit `75b2b42`. Paths and line numbers refer to that revision. The working tree may be checked out on another branch, so read evidence with `git show flightcrew-buildout:<path>` rather than from disk. Where a claim concerns another branch, the branch is named.
"""
P['## Agent Invariants\n']="""
- The launch is the unit of work. The run is the unit of attempt. Neither stands in for the other.
- A spec exists once, in one place, and is referenced from everywhere else by version and commit. No launch, run or tool holds a copy.
- The reader has none of the conversation that produced this document. Every claim here stands on the cited evidence alone.
"""
P['## The target model\n']="""
The layout every problem below is measured against:

```
flightdeck/launch/
  <name>/
    specs/
      interview/
      spec.v1.json
      test-map.v1.json
    runs/
      run-1/
      run-2/
  FLIGHTLOG.md
```

A **launch** is the folder for one piece of work. It is named for the feature it builds and holds two things: the spec series that defines the work, and every run made against that series. A launch is opened once and stays open until a run is accepted. Under the flightcrew v1 system the word launch meant a single attempt; where this document quotes that system, it says so.

A **run** is one attempt at a launch. Runs are numbered in the order they are made and are disposable: a run that fails is ended, diagnosed, and never reopened. The next run starts clean against the same or an amended spec version. A launch accumulates runs until one succeeds.

The **spec series** lives under the launch in `specs/`, beside the runs it drives. Each version is an immutable file. A revision is a new file with the version incremented, never an edit. The `interview/` folder holds the material the spec was grown from: the idea, the questions, the findings, the judge and attacker verdicts. It is never copied anywhere.

**Run outputs** are what a run writes into its own folder: the kickoff version it was given, the plan, the event log, the check outputs, the review findings and the report. Run outputs belong to the run that made them.

**Setup** is what survives runs: the spec series, the tests map, the interview, the kickoff library, the agent definitions and the log. **Output** is what a run produces and a later run does not inherit.

The log is `FLIGHTLOG.md`, one file beside all launches, with one entry per run.
"""
P['### 1. The system names an attempt where the work is a launch\n']="""
**What.** The flightcrew v1 runner creates one folder per attempt and calls it a launch. `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/launch.mjs:267` refuses to open a folder that already exists, `launch exists: <path>`, and the flags it accepts at `launch.mjs:257` offer no override. Its default name, `launch.mjs:231-237`, is the spec name followed by the first free integer. The two completed attempts at building flightcrew were given the names `flightcrew-buildout` and `flightcrew-buildout-2` with the `--name` flag. The log `flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md` heads each entry with the date, the spec name and the folder name, so the entry for the second attempt reads as a run of a different thing rather than the second run of the same thing.

**Why it matters.** Under the target model the folder the runner creates is a run, and the thing it refuses to reuse is correct at that level: a run is never reopened. What is missing is the level above it. Nothing in the system names the launch, so the attempts of one piece of work have no common parent, no shared address, and no count. The refusal that protects a run from being resumed also prevents the work from ever having a home.

**Effect on the system.** Every consumer that should operate on a launch operates on a folder instead. The planner reads the log for prior runs of the same spec by matching the spec name in headings. The next attempt is found by scanning sibling folders. Two attempts at the same feature look identical to two unrelated features that happen to share a spec. The single word the system uses for both concepts hides the distinction from every agent that reads its output.
"""
P['### 2. The spec is copied where it should be pointed at\n']="""
**What.** `fc launch new` copies the spec file into the new folder at `launch.mjs:304-305`, and `fc launch pin tests-map` copies the map the same way. On this branch `flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/spec.v1.json`, `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/specs/flightcrew-v1/spec.v1.json` and `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/specs/flightcrew-v1/spec.v1.json` are the same git blob. Each copy is then added to the run's locked paths, `launch.mjs:443-444`, and the design contract at `flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/design.md:286` records the arrangement as intended: launches hold pinned copies.

The source guides this system was built from never copy the spec. The kickoff guide names the spec by path and frozen commit and says pointers, not copies, so there is exactly one version of the truth. The planning guide's plan header carries the spec as a path at a commit. The spec guide has the run log reference the commit the spec was frozen at.

**Why it matters.** `launch.json` already pins the spec by version and by the commit of the file, so the copy adds nothing the pin does not carry. What it adds is a second and third location where the bytes of the spec exist, each locked separately, each able to drift from the source without any check noticing. A single source of truth is the property the whole method rests on: the orchestrator, the test-builder and the critic must read the same definition of the work. Three files that happen to be identical today are not one file.

**Effect on the system.** Every launch folder is larger than its evidence by the size of the spec and map. The locked-path list of every map includes globs for the copies, so the lock guard and the changed-since-lock check spend effort defending files that should not exist. Under the target model, where the spec series lives inside the launch beside its runs, the copies become copies of a file in the parent folder. The design contract's statement that launches hold pinned copies is the line a planner has to reverse.
"""
P['### 3. The spec-making stage has a home in the model and no owner in the system\n']="""
**What.** The target model gives the interval before a spec is frozen an address: `specs/interview/` under the launch. Nothing in the flightcrew v1 system produces anything at that address. No command under `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/` creates a spec folder, an interview folder or an idea file. The only mention of `interview` in code is `flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/validators/validate-all.mjs:26`, where the validator lists it among directories to skip. The crew README at `flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/README.md:5` and `:28-41` describes a spec-stage dispatcher that passes fixed paths to the spec-builder, including the interview subdirectory. No such dispatcher exists among the twenty command modules. No interviewer role exists on any branch. The file `flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/spec-interviewer.md` is a zero-byte untracked file in the working tree, and `flightdeck/STRUCTURE.md` on branches `main` and `constitution-research` describes it as deliberately empty and the thing the next launch builds.

Every spec in the repository was nonetheless grown by exactly this process, by hand. On branch `constitution-research`, `flightdeck/launch/reference-library/` holds `idea.txt`, `interview/problems.json`, `interview/findings.json`, `interview/bundles/P1.json` through `P5.json`, and `spec.v1.json`. On `engage-crew`, `flightdeck/launch/agent-spec-interviewer/` holds the same shape plus `judge/` and `attacker/` verdicts. The runner accepts the result of that process only once it is a file: `launch.mjs:258-264` requires the spec path to exist and carry a name, and tolerates a draft, deferring the frozen check to `fc launch activate` at `launch.mjs:334-341`.

**Why it matters.** The source guides make the spec-building session stage one of the method, the cheapest exit in the whole process, and the place the human is the main character. It has three roles: an interviewer that asks and never drafts, an attacker in a fresh context, and a judge that rules on readiness. Two of the three exist as crew files on this branch. The stage they belong to has no command, no folder the tooling knows, and no recorded starting point. The interval in which the spec is made is the only interval the system does not model.

**Effect on the system.** Both folders that carry an interview shape have it because the operator knew the shape. Nothing in the repository states it, creates it or would reproduce it. A new launch begins wherever the human puts the first file, and the tooling meets the work only when a frozen spec is handed to it. Under the target model the address exists and is empty, which is an improvement on having no address, and is not yet a stage.
"""
P['### 4. A run branch is recorded and never made\n']="""
**What.** `launch.mjs:288` records a branch name in `launch.json`, defaulting to `run/<name>`, and never creates it. The only later use is at `launch.mjs:571-573`, where a mismatch between the checked-out branch and the recorded one produces a warning. `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/launch.json` records `run/flightcrew-buildout`. No such ref exists locally or on the remote. `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/launch.json` records `flightcrew-buildout-v1`, which is the trunk the buildout branch was later advanced from and which PR #1 merged into it. ------------------------------------------------------------

[ASSISTANT 💬]
Answer to your question first. The three-verdict model is not exit codes. It comes from the testing description manual, which says every check returns exactly one of three signals: an exit code for deterministic checks, a ratio of successes over trials against a pre-declared threshold for statistical checks, and a verdict sheet of scored answers with quotations for judged checks. It was written for agent-shaped artefacts, where behaviour only exists when a model exercises it. Nothing in the built system implements the second or third. Every one of the 58 check entries returns an exit code, the check-result schema allows only pass, fail, error and skipped, and the map schema has no field for a threshold, trial count or rubric. The exit convention you're thinking of is separate: zero for pass, one for usage or environment error, two for a failed check. So the question for the testing document is whether ratio and verdict sheet are a promise to keep or prose to remove.

Your answers to the first three settle the placement rail, and it is a clean one:

1. **Project tests directory.** The project's own assertive tests. Owned by the project, single source of truth, never entered by a run.
2. **Testbench.** Testing artefacts a flightcrew launch needs that do not fit a project tests folder. Fixtures, benches, harnesses. Owned by the deck.
3. **Run checks folder.** Wrappers, one per check in the map, that invoke a test from either of the above and return flightcrew-shaped output. Built by the test-builder after a spec freeze, into the run folder for the attempt they belong to. Locked during that run. Corrected in the next run because verification is a failure axis.
4. **Flightcrew checks, likely renamed verify.** Global wrappers and check libraries every launch shares.

Two consequences worth naming before I dig. The test-builder needs the run folder to exist before it writes, so creating a run becomes the first act of an attempt rather than something that happens after the map is pinned, which reverses the current phase order. And the flightdeck build was self-hosted, so its 29 suites sit in the testbench where under this rail they would be project tests wrapped by checks in the run. Which of those they become is a decision the testing document should record rather than make.

Sending two explorers: one to map exactly what exists at each of the four rail positions on the buildout branch and what invokes what, and one to trace how the current phase order, the test-builder dispatch and the lock interact with a run folder that must exist before the map is written.

[ASSISTANT 💬]
The test-builder does not know how to build them, and the knowledge sits one step upstream of where it is needed.

**What the test-builder is told.** Its role file names the testing description manual as required reading, so it is pointed at the seven classes and the three verdicts. But the only check shape it is taught is one: write each check as a suite that takes no arguments, prints one line per case, and exits 0 or 2. Its return example shows a behavioural exit-code check. The words statistical, judged, ratio, threshold, sample, rubric, probe and scenario appear nowhere in the file. The map template it fills marks class as required only when the spec is agent-shaped, and the schema gives a statistical or judged check no field for a threshold, trial count, rubric or sheet path, so even a builder who understood the classes has nowhere to record what they owe.

**Where the knowledge does live.** Two places, neither in the builder's reach.

- The kickoff part for agent-shaped tasks spells out what each class owes, in one paragraph: deterministic is an exact check run once, property is an invariant over generated cases with generator and seed pinned, statistical is a rate over a fixed sample with sample, threshold and tolerance stated before the run, judged is a rubric a human applies at gate 3 with the verdict appended as a stated event. It also says wave zero delivers the harness the varying classes are measured through: the generator entry point, the fixed sample and the rubric file. That paragraph is read by the orchestrator at plan time, after the map is frozen, and it treats a check missing what its class owes as a spec gap to escalate.
- The spec-builder's rules say that when the product is agent-shaped, the intent or scope text must say so in those words and every behaviour must open with one bracketed class tag, the cheapest that can falsify it.

**Why it never fired.** The flightcrew v1 spec contains neither the phrase agent-shaped nor a single class tag, so the spec-builder rule was not applied, the template's condition for requiring class was never met, the builder wrote exit-code suites for everything including eleven agent definitions, and the orchestrator's kickoff check found no statistical or judged entries to confirm. The whole chain is consistent with itself and consistently missed the artefact it was verifying.

So the answer to your question is the one you guessed. The manuals and the kickoff know the model, the schema cannot carry it, and the builder that must implement it was never taught the shape of a ratio check or a judged check, only where to read about them. The judged class as designed also needs a human at gate 3, which is another way the run's own record shows the model was not exercised: neither run's gate 3 was ever approved.

For the testing document, that lands as one problem with three parts: the spec stage did not tag an agent-shaped spec, the map schema cannot express what the two varying classes owe, and the test-builder has no procedure for either. The explorers still running will give me the placement and phase-order facts. I'll wait for them before proposing the testing document's shape.

## 3. LOCK TIMING

**Lock off during `targets`** — `flightdeck/flightcrew/hooks/lock-guard.mjs:6-13`:
```js
const launch = ctx.launch.json ?? {};
if (launch.phase === 'targets') return 0;
const locked = launch.paths?.locked ?? [];
if (!matchAny(locked, relative)) return 0;
```
So the lock reads `launch.json` `paths.locked` and nothing else.

**`paths.locked` is populated only by pin** — `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/launch.mjs:439-447`:
```js
launchJson.paths = {
  allowed: unique(Array.isArray(map?.allowed_paths) ? map.allowed_paths : []),
  locked: unique([
    ...(Array.isArray(map?.locked_paths) ? map.locked_paths : []),
    `flightdeck/launch/${name}/specs/**`,
    `flightdeck/launch/specs/${specName}/**`,
  ]),
  enforce_boundary: true,
};
```
(Asserted in `flightdeck/testbench/suites/bin-launch/run.mjs:439`: "paths.locked = map locked ∪ launch specs ∪ canonical spec folder".)

**Before a pin, nothing is locked at all**: `paths.locked` is `[]` and `enforce_boundary` is `false` at creation (`launch.mjs:291`), so lock-guard matches nothing and boundary-guard returns early — `flightdeck/flightcrew/hooks/boundary-guard.mjs:23`: `if (!launch.paths?.enforce_boundary) return 0;`. Even after pin, while still in `targets` boundary-guard permits `paths.locked` ∪ the launch folder ∪ the canonical spec home (`boundary-guard.mjs:10-19`, `:14`: `` `flightdeck/launch/specs/${launch.spec.name}/**` ``), documented at `flightdeck/flightcrew/hooks/README.md:13`.

**Base for `fc locked` / `fc boundary`** — `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/boundary.mjs:26-29`: "The commit a change set is measured from: --base, else lock_commit, else base_commit." — `return launchJson?.lock_commit ?? launchJson?.base_commit ?? null;`. `fc locked` reuses it: `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/locked.mjs:10, 29-32` (`baseOf`, `changeSet`, filtered by `launchJson.paths.locked`).

**`lock_commit` is set exactly once, at pin** — `launch.mjs:448`: `launchJson.lock_commit = git.head(ctx.root);`. Schema: `"lock_commit": … "HEAD when the tests map was pinned; the base for boundary, locked and the critic diff."` (`launch.schema.json`). Manual: `launch-anatomy.md:26` "HEAD at `fc launch pin tests-map`; the base for boundary, locked, critic render and 'Changed since lock'". Note `boundary.mjs:17-18`: "A launch's own pinned copies of the spec and the tests map are written one commit after lock_commit by `fc launch pin tests-map`, so counting them as changes would make every run report its own pin as a locked-path change."

## 4. MAP VERSIONING IN PLACE

**Revised map is written beside the previous version, in the same folder** — `flightdeck/manuals/versioning/tests-map-versioning.md:7-13`:
&gt; "A tests map is a sequence of immutable version files beside the spec it maps:
&gt; ```
&gt; specs/&lt;name&gt;/spec.v2.json
&gt; specs/&lt;name&gt;/tests-map.v1.json
&gt; specs/&lt;name&gt;/tests-map.v2.json
&gt; ```"

`:135`: "**To revise**: copy the latest file to the next version number, append the copied file's entry to `previous_versions` …". `:18`: "A version file is never edited after it is frozen. A revision is a new file with `version` incremented."

**Same-folder assumptions**:
- `previous_versions` entries carry a required `file` field naming a sibling: `flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/tests-map.schema.json:34-49` — `"required": ["v", "file", "date", "commit", "reason", "spec"]`, `"file": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }`, description `"Newest first (tm-invariant-9)."` The manual's rule (`tests-map-versioning.md:39-40`): "`previous_versions` follows the header: an append-only list of the headers of every earlier map version, newest first … Entries are never edited or pruned."
- `validate-tests-map.mjs` resolves the pinned **spec** as a sibling of the map first: `flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/validators/validate-tests-map.mjs:92-105` — "The pinned spec file for a map: --spec, else `spec.v&lt;pin version&gt;.json` beside the map, else the launch's spec copy":
```js
const beside = path.join(path.dirname(path.resolve(file)), `spec.v${version}.json`);
if (isFile(beside)) return beside;
```
with a launch fallback via `findLaunchFor` (`:69-90`, walks up to 8 ancestors for a `launch.json`, else resolves `FLIGHTCREW_LAUNCH`/the unique active launch). `tm-invariant-9` itself (`:211-229`) only checks version numbering, not file resolution — it does not open sibling files.
- Canonical home stated in the schema `$id` description: `"launch/specs/&lt;S&gt;/tests-map.vN.json"` (`tests-map.schema.json:5`) and `"name": … "Matches the spec name and the folder under launch/specs/."` (`:28`).
- `launch-anatomy.md:65`: "The canonical spec home is `flightdeck/launch/specs/&lt;S&gt;/` (`spec.v*.json`, `tests-map.v*.json`, `checks/`, `interview/`); a launch holds copies, never the originals."
- `journey.md:94`: "`flightdeck/launch/specs/&lt;S&gt;/` the canonical spec home: spec.v*.json, tests-map.v*.json, checks/; interview/ is never copied".

Under a per-run map, the v1→v2 series would be split across run folders; `previous_versions[].file`, the beside-the-map spec resolution, and the "immutable files beside the spec" rule all assume one folder.

## 5. BASELINE

**When/where**: in phase `targets`, stage 2b, after the test-builder writes the draft map and before the freeze/pin — `launch-anatomy.md:77`, `launch-anatomy.md:94`, `journey.md:20`, `test-builder.md:25`. `journey.md:37`: "The baseline at 2b, where every check fails for the absence of its target, is what proves the target is real."

**What it requires**: only a map file on disk and runnable check commands. `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/check.mjs:28`: "`--baseline` records a draft map's observed baselines before any launch pins it, so it resolves no launch" — `export const needsLaunch = (args) =&gt; !args.includes('--baseline');` (`:29`). `runBaseline` (`check.mjs:312-333`) takes `{ root, mapFile, ids, cwd, launchName }`; there is no launch dir parameter. No pin, no active launch, no launch folder needed — the checks themselves must exist and spawn (`:319-323`, spawn failure → exit 2).

**Where `observed` is written**: **into the map file itself, in place** — `check.mjs:322` `check.baseline.observed = line;`, `:329-331` `map.baseline.commit = head(root) …; writeJsonFile(mapFile, map);`. `check.mjs:310`: "writes no evidence (spec B36)". Evidence files (`evidence/&lt;T&gt;.json`, `summary.json`) are written only by the non-baseline path `runChecks` (`check.mjs:286-305`, `:293-300`), which requires a pinned map (`:388-390`).

Baseline agreement is later re-read from the *pinned copy* by `planBlockers` → `pinnedMap(dir, launchJson)` → `baselineDisagreements(map)` (`launch.mjs:505-512`, `:472-485`).

## Collisions between the current order and the proposed one

The proposal ("run folder first → test-builder writes checks + map *into that run folder* → freeze and pin → implement") agrees with the current system on the first and third steps; every collision is about **step 2's destination**.

1. **The test-builder is told to write outside the run folder.** `crew/test-builder.md:23` mandates `flightdeck/launch/specs/&lt;spec-name&gt;/tests-map.v&lt;n&gt;.json`, and `:22` names `flightdeck/launch/specs/&lt;spec-name&gt;/checks/` as the fallback checks dir. Reinforced by `journey.md:20`, `launch-anatomy.md:65`, `journey.md:94`.
2. **The test-builder is never told the run folder.** Its input list (`test-builder.md:15`) is spec, fixture, codebase, testing manuals — no launch path. The only launch-aware channel for run-chain roles is the kickoff header (`crew/README.md:43`), which at that moment carries `tests-map: (none)` (`journey.md:19`).
3. **Nothing dispatches it programmatically.** There is no `fc test-builder render`; `crew/README.md:5` lists render commands for worker/critic/verifier only, `crew/README.md:28-41` is spec-chain-only, and no file under `flightdeck/flightcrew/workflows/` mentions the role. Any run-scoped path would have to be passed by a human by hand.
4. **`fc launch pin tests-map` re-locks the canonical folder, not a run-local map series.** `launch.mjs:441-445` unconditionally adds `` `flightdeck/launch/specs/${specName}/**` `` alongside the map's own `locked_paths`, and `bin-launch/run.mjs:439` asserts exactly that composition — a run-local map would still lock a folder that, under the proposal, holds nothing for this run.
5. **Pin copies the map to a fixed sub-path of the run folder, from an external source.** `launch.mjs:430` writes `&lt;L&gt;/specs/&lt;specName&gt;/&lt;basename&gt;`. If the map already lives in the run folder, pin copies a file over itself (`fs.copyFileSync`, `:432`) or into a second location, and `boundary.mjs:17-18`'s assumption that "the pinned copies are written one commit after lock_commit" no longer distinguishes the pin from the builder's own output.
6. **Nothing is locked while the map is being written, so "frozen and pinned before implementation" is currently enforced only by the phase-advance refusal, not by the guards.** `launch.mjs:291` (`locked: []`, `enforce_boundary: false`), `lock-guard.mjs:8` (`targets` returns 0), `boundary-guard.mjs:23` (no enforcement until `enforce_boundary`). The only enforcement is `planBlockers` (`launch.mjs:503`) plus `--force` on `fc launch phase` (`:564`).
7. **`lock_commit` is set by pin and is the base for every drift measurement.** `launch.mjs:448`, `boundary.mjs:26-29`, `locked.mjs:29-32`, `launch-anatomy.md:26`. Under a run-local map, the checks the builder wrote inside the run folder would be *inside* `flightdeck/launch/&lt;L&gt;/**`, which `boundary.mjs:42-46` counts as inside the boundary unconditionally — so post-lock edits to run-local checks would not be reported as boundary violations, only as locked-path hits via the `` `flightdeck/launch/${name}/specs/**` `` glob (`launch.mjs:443`), which covers `specs/` only, not a run-local `checks/` dir.
8. **The map version series would fragment across run folders.** `tests-map-versioning.md:7-13` ("immutable version files beside the spec"), `:135` ("copy the latest file to the next version number"), the required `previous_versions[].file` sibling reference (`tests-map.schema.json:39-49`), and `validate-tests-map.mjs:97-98` resolving `spec.v&lt;n&gt;.json` *beside the map* all assume one folder per spec.
9. **Baseline recording writes into the map file in place and resolves no launch.** `check.mjs:29` (`needsLaunch` false with `--baseline`), `:312-331`. It would happily write into a run-local map, but nothing ties the baseline to a run — and the pin later re-reads observed from the *copy* (`launch.mjs:507`), so a run-local map pinned onto itself has no independent pre-pin snapshot.
10. **Hardcoded canonical paths in the guard and the fixtures/suites.** `boundary-guard.mjs:14` permits `flightdeck/launch/specs/&lt;S&gt;/**` during `targets` specifically so the builder can write there; `hooks-guards/run.mjs:176, 322`, `bin-boundary/run.mjs:187-192`, `suite-lib.mjs:267`, `manifest/run.mjs:70,137` and `schemas/run.mjs:32` all assert on that layout, so a move to run-scoped maps changes guard behaviour and breaks these suites.</result>

[ASSISTANT 💬]
The phase-order explorer is back. The key finding corrects an assumption I made a moment ago:

- **The run folder already comes first.** The current order is launch new, then test-builder, then freeze, then pin, then plan. The launch is created with a null map, activate works without one, and the move to plan is what refuses without a pin. So your model does not reverse the phase order. Every collision is about where the test-builder writes, not when.
- **The test-builder is told to write outside the run and is never told the run.** Its four named inputs are spec, fixture, codebase and manuals. No launch path. The map path and the checks fallback are hardcoded to the canonical specs folder. There is no render command for it, no workflow dispatches it, and the human hands it its paths.
- **Nothing is locked while checks are being written.** Locked paths are empty and boundary enforcement is off until pin. The only thing holding "frozen before implementation" is the phase-advance refusal.
- **The run folder is unconditionally inside the boundary.** So checks written inside a run would never register as boundary violations, and the locked glob added at pin covers only the specs subfolder, not a run-local checks folder. A run-local checks folder would be unlocked by both guards.
- **The map series assumes one folder.** Previous-version entries reference sibling files by name, the validator resolves the spec beside the map, and the versioning manual says revisions are copied next to the previous file. Under your model the spec series stays in one folder inside the launch, so the spec side holds. The map side is the question: whether the map lives with the spec series or with the run's checks.
- **Hardcoded paths.** Around forty occurrences of the canonical specs path across the runner, two guards, the settings deny rules, the schema, the template, the fixtures and six locked suites.

That last point about the map sharpens your model. Checks are a run asset because verification is a failure axis. But the map is also the thing that gets versioned, and versioning is how the log's decisions are absorbed. If the map lives in the run with its checks, the series fragments across run folders. If it lives with the spec series, each run's checks are described by a map outside the run. The guides put the map beside the spec. Your model has not said. I'll list it as a decision rather than choose.

The placement explorer is still running. When it lands I'll propose the testing document's shape the same way as structure: a scaffold with the chat summary and headings for you to toggle before any prose.

**`flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-project/` contains** (7 files):
- `README.md`
- `src/export/index.mjs`
- `scripts/export-smoke.mjs`, `scripts/export-invariants.mjs`
- `tests/export/behaviours.test.mjs`, `contract.test.mjs`, `edges.test.mjs`
- `tests/export/fixtures/reference-project.json`

**Yes — something treats its `tests/` as a project suite.** `flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-spec/tests-map.v1.json:40,53,66` names them as check commands:

```
"command": "node --test tests/export/behaviours.test.mjs"   (T2, covers B1–B5)
"command": "node --test tests/export/contract.test.mjs"     (T3, covers I1, I2)
"command": "node --test tests/export/edges.test.mjs"        (T4, covers E1–E3)
```
plus `"run_all": "node --test tests/export/behaviours.test.mjs tests/export/contract.test.mjs tests/export/edges.test.mjs &amp;&amp; node scripts/export-smoke.mjs &amp;&amp; node scripts/export-invariants.mjs"` (`tests-map.v1.json:13`), and `"locked_paths": ["tests/export/**", "flightdeck/launch/specs/export-html/**"]` (line 12).

`flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-project/README.md:3-4`: "Its checks live in `tests/export/` (behaviour, edge and contract tests named by spec id) and `scripts/` (the acceptance smoke and the invariants scan) … Run `node --test` (which finds every `tests/export/*.test.mjs`) and `node scripts/export-smoke.mjs` from this directory; both exit 0 because the implementation is complete."

`flightdeck/testbench/README.md` Fixtures section: "`fixtures/sample-project/`: a small project (`src/export/`, `tests/export/`, `scripts/`) whose checks the sample-spec tests map at `fixtures/sample-spec/tests-map.v1.json` runs; the material every temporary repository is built from."

**"The project's own tests" as distinct from checks — no such notion exists.** `flightdeck/manuals/testing/testing-conventions.md:3` collapses the distinction: "These conventions govern every check in the project — every executable verification that returns a pass or fail." `flightdeck/manuals/testing/testing-description.md:3`: "A check is any executable verification". Unit tests are a *member* of the behavioural class, not a separate rail (`testing-description.md`, Behavioural: "unit tests over enumerable inputs; contract tests on agreed seams; the end-to-end acceptance proof…"). The single phrase in the neighbourhood is `flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/test-builder.md:22`: "the existing test directory the project's checks already live in" — and "the project's own suite protocol document, where it has one".

## 2. TESTBENCH — top-level inventory

| entry | purpose |
|---|---|
| `flightdeck/testbench/README.md` | the suite protocol, run-all contract, fixture roster, bench note and the lock rule |
| `flightdeck/testbench/tests.keep` | directory-keeper + policy: "Test harnesses. reusable across the git branch. save to `main` to access globably. / merge protect this folder. / do not store launch test results here. they belong to each launch. / runs/ is the result of local test runs." |
| `flightdeck/testbench/run-all.mjs` | runs every `suites/*/run.mjs` in name order, hygiene-checks tmpdir + `git status --porcelain`, writes `runs/&lt;suite&gt;.log` and `runs/last.json` |
| `flightdeck/testbench/lib/suite-lib.mjs` | the only file in `lib/`: locations, process runners (`sh`, `fc`, `hook`), temp dirs, fixture builders (`mkLaunchRepo`, `mkActiveLaunch`), assertions (`assert`, `assertEq`, `assertMatch`, `assertIncludes`, `assertExit`), and the `suite()` runner |
| `flightdeck/testbench/suites/` | 29 T-id suite directories, each `run.mjs`, plus helper modules (`constraints/scan-lib.mjs`, `crew/frontmatter.mjs`, `schemas/mini-schema.mjs`, `validate-spec/cases.mjs` + `fixtures/`, `workflows/extract.mjs`) and one non-T suite `unit-integration/` |
| `flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/` | `sample-project/`, `sample-spec/`, `sample-launch/` — the three golden inputs |
| `flightdeck/testbench/benches/rubrics/spec/` | rubric calibration bench: `HARNESS.md`, `collect.mjs`, `render.mjs`, `absorb.mjs`, `rubric-v2-proposal.md`, `two-spec-bench.md`, `experiments/.keep`. "A bench is not a suite: `run-all` does not run it." (README) |
| `flightdeck/testbench/runs/.gitignore` | contents `*` / `!.gitignore` — local run output, gitignored |

### The suite protocol (quoted)

`flightdeck/testbench/README.md`, "## The suite protocol":

&gt; - A suite is `suites/&lt;name&gt;/run.mjs`; it takes no arguments and writes nothing inside the checked-out repository.
&gt; - It prints one line per case, `pass  &lt;case&gt;` or `FAIL  &lt;case&gt;: &lt;reason&gt;`, one `covers: &lt;ids&gt;` line, after the case lines and before the final count, naming the spec node ids it proves (`B`, `C`, `I`, `E` and `SC` ids of the spec above) separated by single spaces, and a final `&lt;n&gt;/&lt;m&gt; passed`.
&gt; - It exits `0` when every case passes and `2` otherwise — only run-all uses exit `1`, for a usage or environment error. An uncaught error becomes a `FAIL` line and exit `2`.
&gt; - Every command under test runs against a temporary repository under `os.tmpdir()`, built by `lib/suite-lib.mjs` (`tmp`, `initRepo`, `mkLaunchRepo`, `mkActiveLaunch`) and removed at exit; child processes run with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, `FLIGHTCREW_ROOT` and `FLIGHTCREW_LAUNCH` scrubbed…
&gt; - Run one suite: `node flightdeck/testbench/suites/&lt;name&gt;/run.mjs`.

`flightdeck/testbench/lib/suite-lib.mjs:1-6` header:

&gt; `// testbench/lib/suite-lib.mjs — shared helpers for every suite under flightdeck/testbench/suites/: locations, process runners, temp directories, fixture builders and assertions.`
&gt; `// Usage: import { suite, fc, hook, sh, tmp, mkLaunchRepo, mkActiveLaunch, assert, assertEq, assertMatch, assertIncludes, assertExit } from '../../lib/suite-lib.mjs'; then await suite('&lt;name&gt;', [{ id, covers: ['B1'], fn: async () =&gt; {} }]).`
&gt; `// Contract (spec I9): a suite prints 'pass  &lt;case&gt;' or 'FAIL  &lt;case&gt;: &lt;reason&gt;' per case, one 'covers: &lt;ids&gt;' line, then '&lt;n&gt;/&lt;m&gt; passed', and exits 0 when every case passed, else 2. It never exits 1 and never crashes: uncaught errors become a FAIL line and exit 2.`

### (a), (b) or (c)?

**Answer: (c) both, but overwhelmingly (a).** The suites *are* the tests of flightdeck-as-a-project — `README.md` §Suites: "One directory per check id of `flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/spec.v1.json` (`T1` `e2e` through `T29` `workflows`; the mapping is the spec's verification text)". They carry the assertions in-process, and they *also* spawn the thing under test (`fc`, the hooks, the validators) as child processes — spawning is how they exercise the subject, not a delegation of the verdict.

**Assertions vs spawning, per suite** (assert-call count / `fc(`,`sh(`,`hook(`,`node(` call count / lines):

| suite | asserts | spawns | lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| bin-launch | 332 | 88 | 1258 |
| bin-dispatch | 133 | 2 | 474 |
| bin-check | 113 | 2 | 463 |
| bin-boundary | 79 | 2 | 343 |
| e2e | 70 | 3 | 249 |
| hooks-stopgate | 64 | 9 | 461 |
| templates | 53 | 5 | 280 |
| bin-report | 48 | 1 | 230 |
| hooks-guards | 47 | 12 | 554 |

| constraints | 40 | 17 | 307 |

| bin-evidence, bin-runlog | 36 | 2 / 8 | 254 / 208 |
| crew | 33 | **0** | 169 |
| bin-distribute | 30 | 2 | 147 |
| bin-plan | 25 | 1 | 130 |
| hooks-structural | 23 | 19 | 248 |
| bin-doctor | 17 | 2 | 138 |

Pure in-process, no child at all: `crew/run.mjs`, `manifest/run.mjs`, `unit-integration/run.mjs`.
The one outlier: `flightdeck/testbench/suites/validate-spec/run.mjs` uses no `assert*` helper — it builds its verdict by hand from a case table and throws (`:48-57`): `if (got.code !== wantCode) problems.push(\`exit ${got.code}, expected ${wantCode}\`)` … `if (problems.length) throw new Error(…)`. It still asserts; it just does not import the helpers. No suite delegates its verdict to another runner.

**Three assertion lines from three suites:**

- `flightdeck/testbench/suites/hooks-stopgate/run.mjs:102` — `assertEq(blocks.length, 1, \`${label}: exactly one stop_block appended\`);`

## 3. RUN CHECKS

### Every command in both maps is a direct suite invocation

`flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/specs/flightcrew-v1/tests-map.v1.json` and `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/specs/flightcrew-v1/tests-map.v2.json` both carry **29 checks, T1–T29, and every single `command` is exactly `node flightdeck/testbench/suites/&lt;name&gt;/run.mjs`**, with `&lt;name&gt;` in this order: `e2e`, `bin-launch`, `hooks-noop`, `hooks-eventlog`, `hooks-guards`, `hooks-structural`, `hooks-stopgate`, `bin-check`, `bin-boundary`, `bin-report`, `bin-evidence`, `bin-runlog`, `bin-plan`, `validate-spec`, `validate-tests-map`, `validate-plan`, `validate-launch`, `lint-spec`, `bin-dispatch`, `bin-distribute`, `bin-doctor`, `crew`, `run-all`, `constraints`, `hook-timing`, `schemas`, `templates`, `manifest`, `workflows`. No exceptions, no flags, no compound shell. Both also carry `"run_all": "node flightdeck/testbench/run-all.mjs"` (v1:66, v2:79) and `"fixture": "flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-project"` (v1:15, v2:28).

### Layers between map command and suite: **none**

`fc check` shells the string directly. `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/check.mjs:129`:
```js
result = spawnSync('/bin/sh', ['-c', String(command)], { cwd, env: childEnv, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: MAX_BUFFER, killSignal: 'SIGKILL' });
```
No wrapper script exists between the map and `run.mjs`. `fc check` itself is the only intermediary, and only as spawner + recorder.

### What `check.mjs` does, exactly

- **Header** (`:1-2`): "runs the checks of the pinned tests map, writes one evidence file per check, rebuilds the evidence summary, and records a draft map's baseline. / Usage: `fc check [all | T1 T2 …] [--cwd &lt;dir&gt;] [--baseline &lt;map-path&gt;]`; exit 0 when nothing failed, 1 on a usage or pin error, 2 when a check failed or errored."
- **Pin**: `pinnedMap()` (`:66-82`) reads `launch.json.tests_map.path`, resolves it inside the launch folder, and compares `map.spec` name/version/commit against `launch.json.spec` — mismatch throws `pin mismatch` (E8), absent pin throws `no tests map pinned` (E11), both exit 1.
- **Spawn** (`runCommand`, `:123-158`): `/bin/sh -c &lt;command&gt;`, `cwd` = launch root or `--cwd`, env = parent env plus `FLIGHTCREW_LAUNCH=&lt;launch name&gt;`, `TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000` (`:13`), `maxBuffer` 16 MiB, `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'`.
- **Capture**: full stdout/stderr, then `tailOf()` keeps `TAIL_LINES = 40` (`:15`, `:100-105`).
- **Write**: `runChecks` (`:286-306`) iterates the selected checks **serially in map order**, writes `launch/&lt;L&gt;/evidence/&lt;T&gt;.json` via `writeJsonFile` (`:300`) in the shape of `check-result.schema.json`: `{ id, command, cwd, exit, verdict, stdout_tail, stderr_tail, duration_ms, ran_at, commit, covers, phase }` (`evidenceOf`, `:168-185`). A quarantined id gets `skippedEvidence` (`:188-203`) with `verdict: 'skipped'`, `exit: null`, empty tails, and **never affects the exit code**.
- **Summary**: `rebuildSummary` (`:232-268`) re-reads *every* `evidence/T*.json` present, sorts by map order, and writes `evidence/summary.json` = `{ ran_at, commit, counts:{pass,fail,error,skipped}, checks:[{id,verdict,covers}], unverified, quarantined, uncovered }`. So `fc check T1 T3` leaves earlier results standing (spec B12).
- **Verdict derivation** (`:144-157`), the whole of it:
```js
if (result.error) cause = ETIMEDOUT ? `${command} was stopped after 300 seconds` : `${command} could not be run: …`;
else if (result.signal) cause = `${command} was killed by ${result.signal}`;
else if (code === 127) cause = `${command} could not be run: no such command`;
else if (code === 126) cause = `${command} could not be run: not executable`;
const verdict = cause !== null ? 'error' : code === 0 ? 'pass' : 'fail';
```
  i.e. **exit 0 → `pass`; any other exit → `fail`; cannot-spawn / 126 / 127 / signal / timeout → `error` with `exit: null`.** No parsing of suite stdout, no `&lt;n&gt;/&lt;m&gt; passed` reading, no ratio.
- **Command exit** (`:305`): `code: red.length &gt; 0 ? EXIT.blocked : EXIT.ok` where red = `fail` or `error`.
- **`--baseline`** (`runBaseline`, `:312-333`): runs a draft map's checks with no pin, sets each `check.baseline.observed` to `` `${verdict}: ${firstLine(stdout, stderr)}` ``, sets `map.baseline.{commit,date}`, **writes no evidence**, exits 2 only if a command failed to spawn.
- `runChecks`/`pinnedMap` are re-imported by `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/verify.mjs:10,55` and `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/worker.mjs:10,174`; `flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/gates/acceptance-gate.mjs:39` spawns `fc check &lt;ids&gt;` as a subprocess.

### Do run folders carry check scripts of their own? **No.**

Neither `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/` nor `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/` has a `checks/` directory or any `.mjs`. `flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/design.md:279` records the deliberate removal: "the existing empty `launch/flightcrew-buildout/checks/` and `specs/` folders are removed first; a `checks/README.md` is not needed".

### What a `checks/` directory under a spec would hold

`flightdeck/launch/README.md`, §Three kinds of entry:
&gt; `specs/&lt;S&gt;/`: the canonical, cross-run home of one spec: `spec.v*.json`, `tests-map.v*.json`, **`checks/` for check scripts with no natural project home**, `interview/`, and any design or reference prose the spec carries. Only `spec.v*.json` and the pinned `tests-map.v*.json` are copied into a launch; `checks/` and `interview/` stay here.

`flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/design.md:20` repeats it verbatim. `flightdeck/manuals/launch/launch-anatomy.md:65`: "The canonical spec home is `flightdeck/launch/specs/&lt;S&gt;/` (`spec.v*.json`, `tests-map.v*.json`, `checks/`, `interview/`); a launch holds copies, never the originals." `flightdeck/manuals/orchestration/journey.md:94` likewise. `flightdeck/manuals/testing/*` does **not** mention a `checks/` directory at all — its placement language is the four addresses (standalone/embedded/chained/enforced), not directories.

The worked example is `flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-spec/checks/boundary-note.md`, whole file:
&gt; This folder is the spec's own home for check scripts that have no natural place in the project: a scan that spans several source trees, a golden comparison, a script the map's commands call by the path `flightdeck/launch/specs/export-html/checks/&lt;name&gt;`. It sits inside `flightdeck/launch/specs/export-html/**`, which the tests map locks, so nothing here changes during a run. The export-html checks all have a project home (`tests/export/` for the behaviour, edge and contract tests, `scripts/` for the smoke and invariants scripts), so this folder holds only this note; a later map revision that needs a cross-tree check puts the script here and names it in the spec's verification text.

`flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/test-builder.md:22` gives the placement precedence: "Write each check as a suite in the first of these that applies: the directory your dispatch names, else the existing test directory the project's checks already live in, else `flightdeck/launch/specs/&lt;spec-name&gt;/checks/`."

## 4. FLIGHTCREW CHECKS — full inventory of `flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/`

`checks.keep`, in full: **"Universal check harnesses, infrastructure for every launch."**

**`validators/` (8 files)** — each runnable standalone or via `fc validate` / `fc lint`:

| file | purpose (own header line 1) |
|---|---|
| `validate-spec.mjs` | validates one spec against `spec.schema.json` and the thirteen coded invariants |
| `validate-tests-map.mjs` | validates one tests map against `tests-map.schema.json`, the thirteen map invariants and the coverage rule |
| `validate-plan.mjs` | validates one plan against `plan.schema.json` + plan rules, resolving pinned map, spec and ceilings |
| `validate-launch.mjs` | validates one `launch.json` against `launch.schema.json` plus the rules the schema cannot express |
| `validate-return.mjs` | validates one stored agent return against the schema of its kind (worker/explorer/verifier/critic) |
| `validate-kickoff.mjs` | validates a rendered `kickoff.md`: header fields, pointers, crew names |
| `validate-all.mjs` | runs every validator over every document of a directory tree |
| `spec-readiness-lint.mjs` | the readiness rules a spec passes before a human freezes it (nine domains, id sequences, class tags…) |

**`gates/` (3 files)**:

| file | purpose |
|---|---|
| `acceptance-gate.mjs` | "the gate of the verify phase: it runs the pinned tests map's acceptance check through `fc check`" — exports `run(context)`, `runFcCheck`, `evidenceFor`, `acceptanceId`, `gateContext` |
| `contracts-gate.mjs` | "the gate of the contracts phase: it runs the checks of the plan's contracts unit (the acceptance check when the plan declares `no_contracts`) and the boundary" |
| `structural-gate.mjs` | "runs the active launch's structural command for one file's extension" — exit 0 sound / 2 command failed / 1 no launch |

**`lib/` (7 files)** — pure libraries, imported by everything including `bin/cmd/*`:
`schema-lib.mjs` (the JSON-Schema subset checker), `spec-lib.mjs` (spec node index + thirteen invariants), `launch-lib.mjs` (root/launch resolution, `launch.json`, `events.jsonl`, `escalation.json`), `git-lib.mjs` (read-only git that never throws), `glob-lib.mjs` (the allowed/locked path glob dialect), `output.mjs` ("the one place every fc command, validator, gate and hook writes a line… and the three exit codes"), `render-lib.mjs` (HTML/markdown rendering helpers).

Plus `checks.keep`. **No other entries.**

### Who invokes what

- **By hooks**: `flightdeck/flightcrew/hooks/stop-gate.mjs:44-45` loads a gate by URL — `` const url = new URL(`../checks/gates/${name}.mjs`, import.meta.url); `` — running `acceptance-gate` in phase `verify` and `contracts-gate` in phase `contracts` (`design.md:256`). `structural-gate.mjs` is the PostToolUse structural path (`flightcrew/README.md:12`: "`acceptance-gate`, `contracts-gate`, `structural-gate`: what the stop gate and the structural hook run"). `hooks/README.md:42`: "Each exports `run(context)` and returns `{ ran, reason?, checks: […], extra: [...] }` … A gate that is missing or throws is logged and treated as 'could not run', never as a failure."
- **By fc commands**: `bin/cmd/validate.mjs:1` ("runs one validator from `flightcrew/checks/validators/`"), `bin/fc.mjs:192` (runs a validator or linter as a program), `bin/cmd/doctor.mjs:182` (checks `validate-launch.mjs` is installed). All of `bin/cmd/*` import from `checks/lib/`.
- **By crew**: `flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/README.md:33-34` — "validator, run by spec-builder: `…/validate-spec.mjs`", "linter, run by spec-builder: `…/spec-readiness-lint.mjs`".
- **By suites**: `testbench/suites/validate-spec/run.mjs:10` spawns `validate-spec.mjs` directly; `lint-spec` spawns `spec-readiness-lint.mjs`; `validate-launch`, `validate-plan`, `validate-tests-map` suites exercise them through `fc`; `manifest/run.mjs:46-47` asserts all eight validators and three gates are listed in `MANIFEST.txt`; `unit-integration/run.mjs:84` asserts `/checks\/gates\//.test(hook)`.

### Is anything in `checks/` a "check" in the tests-map sense?

**No.** Nothing under `flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/` appears as a `command` in any tests map on this branch — all 58 check commands across both maps are `node flightdeck/testbench/suites/&lt;name&gt;/run.mjs`. The `validators/` and `gates/` are the *subjects under test* (T14–T18 are their regression suites) and the *machinery hooks call*; `lib/` is pure library. The directory name is aspirational infrastructure — "Universal check harnesses" — not an inventory of map-level checks.

## 5. WRAPPING — no example of a check wrapping an external test runner

Grep across `flightdeck/` for `npm test`, `npx`, `yarn test`, `pnpm test`, `rspec`, `pytest`, `go test`, `cargo test`, `node --test`, `jest`, `vitest`, `mocha`, `bundle exec`:

- **No `.mjs` under `flightdeck/flightcrew/` or `flightdeck/testbench/suites/` invokes any of them.** Zero hits.
- The only *executable* hits are in the fixture: `flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-project/tests/export/{behaviours,contract,edges}.test.mjs` are themselves `node --test` files (headers: "Usage: node --test tests/export/behaviours.test.mjs (from the project root)").
- The only *map* hits are the fixture maps: `flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-spec/tests-map.v1.json:40,53,66` and its copy `flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-launch/specs/export-html/tests-map.v1.json:61,77,94` — `"command": "node --test tests/export/…"`. Their recorded evidence at `flightdeck/testbench/fixtures/sample-launch/evidence/T2.json:3` etc. carries the same command string with `"observed": "pass: TAP version 13"` in the map's baseline.
- One mention as a *token list*, not an invocation: `flightdeck/flightcrew/checks/validators/spec-readiness-lint.mjs:43` — `'make', 'cargo', 'go', 'java', 'dotnet', 'php', 'pytest', 'jest', 'vitest', 'mocha', 'tap', 'git',` — a vocabulary of command names the linter recognises in spec text.

**So: the "wrapping" pattern exists only as `command: "node --test &lt;file&gt;"` in a fixture map — a bare invocation, no translation layer.** `fc check` performs the entire translation (exit 0 → `pass`, non-zero → `fail`, cannot-spawn → `error`); nothing intermediate parses TAP or a runner's summary. Note `runBaseline`'s `firstLine()` captures `"pass: TAP version 13"` — the first line of TAP output — which is the only place a runner's stdout is read at all, and it is recorded as prose, not interpreted.

`flightdeck/flightcrew/templates/tests-map.template.json` says nothing about existing project tests; its `command` field reads: `"&lt;command run as /bin/sh -c from the launch root; never shown to a worker&gt;"`, and `"fixture": "&lt;path to the fixture the checks run against&gt;"`. The only shape guidance is the `kind` enum `"&lt;structural | behavioural | artefact | invariant | project-rule | statistical | judged&gt;"` and `class` `"&lt;deterministic | property | statistical | judged&gt;"`.

`flightdeck/flightcrew/crew/test-builder.md` step 2 is the closest thing to a policy on a project's existing tests:
&gt; Write each check as a suite in the first of these that applies: the directory your dispatch names, else **the existing test directory the project's checks already live in**, else `flightdeck/launch/specs/&lt;spec-name&gt;/checks/`. A suite takes no arguments, prints one line per case, and exits 0 or 2; the project's own suite protocol document, where it has one, carries the rest of the contract.

That is a *placement* instruction (write new suites into the existing directory), not a wrapping one. Nothing tells the test-builder to invoke an existing runner and adapt it; step 5 requires only that "Every command must spawn", and the returned shape (`test-builder.md`, "What you return") is `{ "command": "node path/to/suite/run.mjs", … }`.

---

## 6. VERDICTS

### The schema enum

`flightdeck/flightcrew/schemas/check-result.schema.json:13`:
```json
"verdict": { "type": "string", "enum": ["pass", "fail", "error", "skipped"] },
```
and `:12`: `"exit": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "description": "null when the command could not spawn or was killed." }`. The schema `description` (`:6`) states the execution contract: "Each check runs as `/bin/sh -c &lt;command&gt;` with cwd the launch root (or `--cwd`), the parent environment plus `FLIGHTCREW_LAUNCH`, a 300 second limit, serially in map order; a command that cannot spawn or times out has verdict error, a null exit and a `stderr_tail` naming the command and the cause."

### Derivation from exit code

`flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/check.mjs:156`:
```js
const verdict = cause !== null ? 'error' : code === 0 ? 'pass' : 'fail';
```
with `cause` set (`:144-155`) by: `result.error` ETIMEDOUT → "was stopped after 300 seconds"; other `result.error` → "could not be run"; `result.signal` → "was killed by &lt;signal&gt;"; `code === 127` → "no such command"; `code === 126` → "not executable". The fourth verdict, `skipped`, is assigned without running anything, only for a quarantined id (`skippedEvidence`, `:188-203`), and `runChecks:304` counts only `fail`/`error` as red.

### Exit code conventions

`flightdeck/launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/design.md:12` (the line quoted, in full):
&gt; - Runtime: Node 22 ES modules (`.mjs`), only `node:` built-in imports and relative imports inside `flightcrew/` or `testbench/`, no `package.json`, no `jq`. macOS. Success prints one line; failure prints specific lines. **Exit codes: `0` pass, `1` usage or environment error, `2` failed check or blocking decision.**

`flightdeck/testbench/README.md`, §The suite protocol:
&gt; - It exits `0` when every case passes and `2` otherwise — only run-all uses exit `1`, for a usage or environment error. An uncaught error becomes a `FAIL` line and exit `2`.

§run-all:
&gt; `node flightdeck/testbench/run-all.mjs [--only &lt;substring&gt;]` … exits `0` when every suite passes, `1` on a usage or environment error (including no suites at all), `2` otherwise.

Same convention in `bin/cmd/check.mjs:2` ("exit 0 when nothing failed, 1 on a usage or pin error, 2 when a check failed or errored"), each gate's usage header, and `flightdeck/flightcrew/README.md` ("exit `0` on success, `1` on a usage or environment error, `2` on a failed check or a blocking decision").

### Ratio / threshold / verdict sheet: **no code path anywhere under `flightdeck/` reads one**

Grepped `ratio|threshold|verdict[ _-]sheet` case-insensitively across every `.mjs` and `.js` under `flightdeck/`, and across `flightcrew/schemas/*.json` and `flightcrew/templates/*`. Every hit is a false positive on `duration_ms`, `gate_iterations`, `integration_check`, `enumeration`, `migration`, `iterations`. In particular:

The concepts exist **only in prose**:

Fair. Plain words.

A check runs a command. When the command finishes, the operating system hands back a number called the exit code. Zero means it worked, anything else means it did not. That is the whole signal flightcrew's runner reads. It looks at the number, records pass for zero, fail for anything else, and error if the command could not start at all. It never reads what the command printed.

The manuals ask for more than that. They say a check can return one of three things:

- **An exit code.** Pass or fail, as above. This is what a normal test does.
- **A ratio.** Run the same scenario many times, count how often the behaviour happened, compare that against a threshold you wrote down beforehand. Se
