## 1. THE END COMMAND — `flightdeck/flightcrew/bin/cmd/launch.mjs`

**Signature** (`launch.mjs:34`): `fc launch end &lt;outcome&gt; [--at &lt;stage&gt;] [--units U,...]`. Flags parsed at `launch.mjs:784`: `{ at: 'string', units: 'string' }` — those two only. Outcome is positional and must be in `OUTCOMES = ['accepted', 'accepted-with-reservations', 'abandoned', 'partial']` (`launch.mjs:41`, checked `launch.mjs:786`).

**Preconditions, in read order (all reads happen before the first write — `launch.mjs:9`: "A refusal writes nothing"):**

1. Outcome valid → else `UsageError` → exit 1 (`launch.mjs:786`).
2. `partial` requires `--units` non-empty → `UsageError`, exit 1 (`launch.mjs:790-793`).
3. **Accepted family only** (`ACCEPTED_FAMILY = ['accepted','accepted-with-reservations','partial']`, `launch.mjs:42`; note `partial` is in the accepted family here, `abandoned` never is):
   - `evidence/summary.json` must exist: `no evidence: evidence/summary.json is absent, HEAD is &lt;sha&gt;; run fc verify` → `BlockedError`, exit 2 (`launch.mjs:799`).
   - `summary.commit` must equal HEAD: `evidence is stale: evidence/summary.json is at X, HEAD is Y` → exit 2 (`launch.mjs:800-802`).
   - Tree clean under `launch.paths.allowed`, **excluding the launch's own folder** (`launch.mjs:805-809`): `const ownFolder = ['flightdeck/launch/${name}/**']` … `working tree not clean under allowed paths: &lt;paths&gt;` → exit 2. Comment at `launch.mjs:803-804`: "The launch's own folder is the run's record and is always writable to the run (design section 4), so its evidence, returns and report never make the tree unclean for the ending."
4. **Partial only**: `plan.json` must exist (`a partial ending needs plan.json to know the units`, exit 2) and `partialBlockers` must be empty → `partial ending refused:` + one indented line per problem, exit 2 (`launch.mjs:811-815`).

Not checked anywhere: the phase (any phase may end; the suite's `end-abandoned-records-and-renders` patches phase to `report` only for realism), gate status (see §9), whether a trigger is fired, whether the critic converged, whether `notes.md` exists.

**What it writes** (`launch.mjs:817-830`): `launch.json` gets `outcome`, `status` (= outcome), `ended` (ISO now), `phase = 'ended'`, plus `accepted_units`/`abandoned_units` on partial; then `writeLaunch`, then `appendEvent(dir, { event: 'launch_end', phase: 'ended', detail: { outcome, at: flags.at ?? null } })`, then `clearEscalation(dir)` (deletes `escalation.json` — suite assertion `end removes escalation.json`, `bin-launch/run.mjs:944`).

Then three renders, each individually try/caught, each failure downgrading the exit code to 1 but not aborting (`launch.mjs:832-852`): `renderThrough(evidence.mjs)` → `evidence.html`; `renderThrough(report.mjs)` → `report.md`; `writeStub(ctx)` → the RUNLOG entry. Failure messages: `the evidence page could not be rendered: …`, `report.md could not be rendered: …`, `the run-log stub could not be inserted: …`. It does **not** write `notes.md` (only `fc launch note`, `launch.mjs:671-680`).

**What it prints** (`launch.mjs:854-855`): the two cleanup lines then the report path. The lines are built by `cleanupLines` (`launch.mjs:770-785`):

```js
lines.push(worktrees.length &gt; 0
  ? `worktrees to remove: ${worktrees.map((p) =&gt; `git worktree remove ${repoPath(ctx, p)}`).join(' · ')}`
  : 'worktrees to remove: none');
lines.push(branches.length &gt; 0
  ? `branches to delete: ${branches.map((branch) =&gt; `git branch -D ${branch}`).join(' · ')}`
  : 'branches to delete: none');
```

Worktrees are those from `git worktree list` whose path contains `/.claude/worktrees/`; branches are synthesised as `${launchJson.name}/${unit.name ?? unit.id}` for every unit in `plan.json` — i.e. printed whether or not the branch exists.

**It deletes nothing and removes nothing.** No `git worktree remove`, `git branch -D`, or `git worktree prune` is executed anywhere in the command; the strings are printed for the human. (`git worktree prune` appears in no `.mjs` on the branch — only in `endings.md:27,74` prose.)

**Exit codes**: 0 normally; 1 (`EXIT.usage`) on bad outcome/missing `--units`, or if any of the three renders threw; 2 (`EXIT.blocked`) on stale evidence, dirty tree, missing plan, or refused partial. Mapping: `fc.mjs:347-353` (`UsageError`→1, `BlockedError`→2); `EXIT = { ok: 0, usage: 1, blocked: 2 }` (`output.mjs:15`).

**G3 is not required.** See §9.

## 2. OUTCOMES, `--at`, `--units`

| outcome | evidence/clean-tree gate | extra writes | RUNLOG family |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accepted` | yes (`launch.mjs:796-810`) | — | `kept: &lt;fill&gt;`, `reservation: &lt;fill&gt;` |
| `accepted-with-reservations` | yes | — | same as accepted (`runlog.mjs:23,101-102`) |
| `partial` | yes, **plus** `partialBlockers` | `accepted_units`, `abandoned_units` | abandoned/partial family + `landed:`/`abandoned:` |
| `abandoned` | none — always accepted | — | abandoned family |

`--at &lt;stage&gt;` is a free string; it is validated against nothing and stored nowhere in `launch.json`. It goes only into the event detail: `appendEvent(dir, { event: 'launch_end', … detail: { outcome, at: flags.at ?? null } })` (`launch.mjs:829`). It resurfaces only through `runlog.mjs:50-52`, which reads the last `launch_end` event and builds `` `${outcome}${at ? ` at ${at}` : ''}` `` as the head of the `symptom` line. Matches `run-log.md:35`: "the `--at` stage is recorded in the ending event and surfaces in the pre-filled `symptom`, not in `outcome`".

`--units` is a comma list of **unit ids** (`launch.mjs:792`). `partialBlockers` (`launch.mjs:732-769`) refuses, one line per problem, when: an id is not a unit of the plan; a kept unit `depends_on` an id neither kept nor the `kind: contracts` unit ("`X depends on Y, which is not among the units kept`"); a kept unit has neither `returns/&lt;id&gt;.json.status === 'green'` nor a `unit_merged` event ("`X has no green worker return and no unit_merged event`"); an open blocking finding's `file` matches the unit's `paths` ("`X has the open blocking finding F under its paths (file)`"). Finding state is pass files overlaid with `review/resolutions.json` (`launch.mjs:711-731`).

Recording (`launch.mjs:822-827`): `accepted_units = keep` verbatim; `abandoned_units` = every other plan unit id — derived, not given. Both are optional string arrays in `schemas/launch.schema.json:141-142`. `report.mjs:100-103` prints `accepted units: … abandoned units: …` in the header when either is non-empty; `runlog.mjs:106-109` emits `landed:`/`abandoned:` lines (with `—` when empty).

## 3. LAND — `fc launch land`

`launch.mjs:681-706`. Flags `--commit`, `--pr`, `--evidence-commit`. Preconditions: `--commit` required (exit 1); `evidence/summary.json.commit` must match `--evidence-commit` (defaulting to `--commit`) → `no evidence at &lt;sha&gt;: evidence/summary.json records &lt;sha&gt;` exit 2; `counts.fail` and `counts.error` must both be 0 → `evidence at &lt;sha&gt; records N failed and M errored checks` exit 2. It does **not** check `outcome`, `phase`, `ended`, gates, or that a merge happened.

Writes:

```js
launchJson.landed = {
  commit: landedCommit,
  pr: flags.pr ?? null,
  integration_check: `evidence/summary.json @ ${shortHash(evidenceCommit)}: ${counts.pass ?? 0} passed, 0 failed, 0 errored`,
};
```

then `writeLaunch`, `bestEffortRender`, `ok('landed at &lt;sha&gt; · &lt;pr&gt;')`, exit 0. No event is appended for landing. `validate-launch.mjs:75` only resolves `landed.commit` as a hash; `report.mjs:97-99` echoes `landed: &lt;commit&gt; · &lt;pr&gt; · &lt;integration_check&gt;` in the report header.

**Nothing merges.** No `fc` command merges to a parent branch; `fc worker merge &lt;unit&gt;` merges unit branches into the run branch during the run only. The merge is the human's, per `journey.md:31` (stage 10, "Who: human"): "integration branch rebased on the parent, `fc verify` there, PR opened with `report.md` linked, CI, merge, `fc launch land --commit &lt;sha&gt; --pr &lt;url&gt;`". Integration/rebase exists **only in prose**: `endings.md:70` ("rebase the run branch (`launch.json.branch`) or an integration branch built from it onto the current parent; run `fc verify` there"), `endings.md:73,94,104`, `journey.md:31`, and the launch template's description of `branch` (`templates/launch.template.json:26`: `"&lt;integration branch for this run, run/&lt;name&gt; by default&gt;"`). No command creates, rebases, or verifies an integration branch; `fc verify` has no branch argument.

## 4. THE RUN LOG STUB

`bin/cmd/runlog.mjs`; `templates/runlog-entry.template.md`.

`stubEntry` (`runlog.mjs:90-115`) — mechanical, always filled: heading `## &lt;ended[0:10]&gt; · &lt;spec.name&gt; · &lt;launch.name&gt;`; `spec: &lt;name&gt; v&lt;version&gt; @ &lt;commit|draft&gt;`; `kickoff: &lt;kickoff.version|(none)&gt;`; `outcome:`; `cost: ${costLine(counts)}` from `countBudget`. Then by family:

- Accepted family = `['accepted','accepted-with-reservations']` (`runlog.mjs:23`): `kept: &lt;fill&gt;`, `reservation: &lt;fill&gt;`.
- Everything else (i.e. `abandoned` **and** `partial`): `symptom:` pre-filled by `symptomOf`, then `for (const field of ['seen on','cause','fixed on','change','watch']) lines.push(`${field}: ${FILL}`)`; partial adds `landed:`/`abandoned:`; then `kept: &lt;fill&gt;`, `promote: &lt;fill&gt;` — emitted unconditionally in this branch, though `runlog-entry.template.md:21` and `run-log.md:35` call `kept`/`promote` "optional lines the human adds".
- `observations:` bullets from the newest `review/pass-N.json`, `kind === 'observation'` findings only (`runlog.mjs:69-84,112-113`).

`symptomOf` (`runlog.mjs:47-67`): `&lt;outcome&gt;[ at &lt;--at&gt;]` — ` — ` — newest of {gate exit | escalation | trigger} rendered — ` — ` — `units abandoned: …` on partial.

Insertion (`insertEntry`, `runlog.mjs:118-140`): finds the first line starting `# `, writes `before + blank + entry + rest` — newest first; creates the file with `# Run log\n\n&lt;entry&gt;` when no `# ` heading exists. `writeStub` (`runlog.mjs:143-149`) refuses when the launch has not ended: `the launch has not ended; run fc launch end before fc runlog stub`.

`fc runlog show [--spec S]` (`runlog.mjs:168-189`): splits on `## ` headings in file order (which is newest-first), filters with `entry.heading.includes(' · ' + flags.spec + ' · ')`, prints each entry then a blank line; prints `no run log yet` / `no entries for spec S` and exits 0.

**Is any `&lt;fill&gt;` ever enforced? No.** The full `&lt;fill&gt;` grep across `flightdeck/` returns only: `runlog.mjs:5,22`; `templates/runlog-entry.template.md:15,16,30-34,37,38`; `launch/README.md:29`; `launch/RUNLOG.md:32`; three copies of spec node B-text (`launch/*/specs/flightcrew-v1/spec.v1.json:317`, `launch/specs/…:317`); `launch/specs/flightcrew-v1/design.md:170`; `manuals/launch/launch-anatomy.md:101`; `manuals/orchestration/run-log.md:34,35,60`; `testbench/suites/bin-runlog/run.mjs:4,81,88,106`. The only mechanical assertions are in the testbench, and they assert the **opposite** direction: `assertEq(field(lines, name), '&lt;fill&gt;', …)` (line 81) requires the field to *be* `&lt;fill&gt;` at stub time. Nothing — no validator (`validate-launch`, `validate-plan`, `validate-all`), no hook (`stop-gate`, `session-end`, `lock-guard`, `boundary-guard`), no suite, no `fc launch new` / `fc launch activate` / `fc launch pin` precondition — reads RUNLOG for completeness or refuses while a `&lt;fill&gt;` remains. `fc launch new` never reads RUNLOG at all (`launch.mjs:256-315`); `fc launch activate` refuses only on another *active* launch, unfrozen pins and pin mismatch (`launch.mjs:316-355`). The only RUNLOG-reading validation anywhere is `validate-plan.mjs:115-125,289-301`, and it is a **warning** that a `source: runlog` risk names an existing heading — heading text only, never a field value.

Evidence the rule is unenforced: `launch/RUNLOG.md:24-30` — the abandoned entry's judgement fields all read `seen on: draft (orchestrator): verification`, `cause: draft (orchestrator): …`, `fixed on: …`, `change: …`, `watch: …`, `kept: …`, `promote: …`, and the accepted entry's `kept:`/`reservation:` likewise (`RUNLOG.md:8-9`). An agent wrote every `&lt;fill&gt;` field, against `run-log.md:60` ("An agent never writes a `&lt;fill&gt;` field"), and nothing refused.

Also note `RUNLOG.md:32`: the file's explanatory sentence sits *below* the entries, because `insertEntry` pushes entries directly under `# Run log` and shoves the prose down.

## 5. THE MANUAL — `manuals/orchestration/endings.md` (106 lines) + `run-log.md`

Ending procedure, step by step, with actor:

**Framing** (`endings.md:3`): "A run is over the moment trust in it stops. Every run ends one of three ways, across four `fc launch end` outcomes." `endings.md:15-17`: accepted family refused on stale evidence/dirty tree, "`abandoned` is always accepted"; "Every ending sets `outcome`, `status`, `ended` and phase `ended`, renders `report.md` and `evidence.html`, inserts the RUNLOG stub, appends `launch_end`, and prints the worktree and branch cleanup lines and the report path"; "Momentum never decides an ending; triggers written at planning time do."

**Abandon sequence** (`endings.md:23-27`) — five steps, exactly the prescribed shape:
1. *Stop at the finding* — enforced by hooks + `fc` refusals (`fc worker render`, `fc worker merge`, `fc launch phase` except to ended, "exit 2"); actor: mechanism + orchestrator ("dispatch nothing new").
2. *Freeze the evidence* — human types `fc launch end abandoned --at &lt;gate|stage&gt;`; fc renders.
3. *Write the run-log entry* — human: "fill `seen on`, `cause`, `fixed on`, `change`, `watch` now, not later."
4. *Make the setup change* — human: spec node, kickoff part, hook, critic mandate, check; "commit it together with the log entry so the fix and its reason travel together."
5. *Clear the ground* — human: "run the printed cleanup lines (`git worktree remove`, `git branch -D &lt;L&gt;/&lt;unit&gt;`), `git worktree prune`; a failed unit is a discarded directory."

Plus `endings.md:29-30`: "Do not resume the abandoned session and do not carry its transcript forward; the next orchestrator meets the failure only through the run log, as a risk line in the new plan."

**Merge sequence** (`endings.md:69-75`), all human: wave order via `fc worker merge` during the run, "the merge to the parent branch extends the same order"; "Integrate before the trunk: rebase the run branch (`launch.json.branch`) or an integration branch built from it onto the current parent; run `fc verify` there"; "Open the PR from that branch with `flightdeck/launch/&lt;L&gt;/report.md` linked; let CI run the same gates"; "Merge, then `fc launch land --commit &lt;sha&gt; --pr &lt;url&gt; [--evidence-commit &lt;sha&gt;]`"; "Land it readable: one squashed commit per unit or one commit per merge"; "Close the run: fill the run-log fields, prune worktrees, delete `&lt;L&gt;/*` branches, promote confirmed rules; the ground is clear for the next run."

**Cleanup / branches / worktrees**: `endings.md:27,74,95`, `endings.md:106` ("The haunted repository: worktrees and branches from abandoned runs still standing; abandonment ends with clear ground"), `launch-anatomy.md:101` ("run the worktree and branch cleanup lines `fc launch end` printed"). All human, all raw git.

**Human diagnosis**: `run-log.md:60`: "The orchestrator reads the log and carries its risks into the plan. The human writes `seen on`, `cause`, `fixed on`, `change` and `watch`, and commits the entry. An agent never writes a `&lt;fill&gt;` field." Also `run-log.md`, Practice: "Let `fc` draft and the human diagnose: the stub fills spec, kickoff, outcome, cost and symptom; the axis, the cause and the change are judgements the run could not make."

**Every `fc` command a human types at the ending, per the manuals** (endings.md + run-log.md + journey stage 10 + launch-anatomy "after" row):
1. `fc launch gate &lt;G&gt; exit` (abandon at a gate, `endings.md:12`; the command then prints `now run: fc launch end abandoned --at G1`, `launch.mjs:648`)
2. `fc launch end accepted`
3. `fc launch end accepted-with-reservations`
4. `fc launch end abandoned --at &lt;gate|stage&gt;`
5. `fc launch end partial --units U1,U3`
6. `fc verify` (on the rebased integration branch, `endings.md:70,94`)
7. `fc launch land --commit &lt;sha&gt; --pr &lt;url&gt; [--evidence-commit &lt;sha&gt;]`
8. `fc runlog show [--spec S]` (`run-log.md`, `launch-anatomy.md:101`)
9. `fc runlog stub` ("re-inserts a stub by hand when needed", run-log.md)

That is **9 distinct `fc` invocations**, of which only **4 are on any single ending path** (one `end` form + `fc verify` + `fc launch land` + `fc runlog show`; the abandon path is 1 `end` + `fc runlog show`, or 2 with a gate exit). Everything else at the ending is git, gh/PR UI, and text editing.

**Promotion pass** at the ending: `endings.md:74` "promote confirmed rules"; `journey.md:31` stage title "Merge, log, promote"; procedure only in `run-log.md` §Promotion (see §11).

## 6. WHAT SURVIVES an abandoned run

Per code: **everything is kept**. `fc launch end abandoned` deletes nothing, archives nothing, moves nothing. The launch folder stays in place under `flightdeck/launch/&lt;L&gt;/` with `kickoff.md`, `plan.json/md`, `specs/&lt;S&gt;/spec.vN.json` (the pinned copy), `tests-map.vN.json`, `returns/`, `review/`, `evidence/`, `evidence.html`, `report.md`, `events.jsonl`, `notes.md`. Both recorded runs demonstrate this: `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/` is fully intact on the branch with `status: abandoned`. `flightdeck/blackbox/archive.keep` exists as an empty placeholder; no command writes there — **no archiving anywhere**.

Deleted, per manual and by the human's hand only: the per-unit worktrees under `.claude/worktrees/` and the `&lt;L&gt;/&lt;unit&gt;` branches (`endings.md:27,74,95`). The run branch (`launch.json.branch`) is not named for deletion; `journey.md` "Exits and re-entry" says "The branch is left as it is".

**The salvage rule is stated, as a table** — `endings.md:32-42`, "What a failed run may leave behind", column "carries over": spec **yes** ("setup; unless `fixed on` names the context axis and the change is to the spec, in which case the amended spec re-frozen at a new commit carries instead"); tests map and check scripts **yes**; wave-0 contracts **if proven**; explorer returns **if factual** ("'the renderer lives in X' survives; conclusions drawn for the failed approach do not"); `plan.json` **no** ("per-run by design; the next plan is generated fresh with the failure as a `source: runlog` risk"); partial implementation on `&lt;L&gt;/&lt;unit&gt;` branches **no** ("reading it to save time imports its assumptions"); orchestrator transcript **no**. Restated as a checklist item at `endings.md:89`: "Salvage passed the setup-versus-output test of the carries-over table above — setup carries, run output does not". Anti-pattern `endings.md:101`: "Salvaging the diff". **No code enforces any row of this table.**

## 7. THE RETRY

Mechanically: `fc launch new &lt;spec&gt;` again (`launch.mjs:256-315`). If `--name` is omitted, `defaultName` picks `&lt;specName&gt;-&lt;n&gt;` for the first free `n` (`launch.mjs:232-238`) — which is why run 2 is `flightcrew-buildout-2` (the human passed a name for run 1). `previous_launch` is filled automatically by `previousLaunch` (`launch.mjs:240-254`): the newest *other* launch with the same `spec.name`, by `created` then `launch.json` mtime then name — it does **not** require the previous launch to have ended, and does not chain more than one back. Confirmed: `flightcrew-buildout-2/launch.json` `"previous_launch": "flightcrew-buildout"`; run 1 has `null`.

What carries automatically into the new launch: **only the `previous_launch` string and a kickoff header line**. `renderKickoff` (`launch.mjs:161-184`) emits:

```
read first: flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md    prior reports: &lt;prior report paths or none&gt;
```

`priorReports` (`launch.mjs:145-159`) lists `report.md` of every other launch of the same spec. Confirmed in `flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout-2/kickoff.md:4`: `read first: flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md    prior reports: flightdeck/launch/flightcrew-buildout/report.md`. The render **never opens RUNLOG.md** — it only prints its path; nothing from the previous entry (`change`, `watch`, `fixed on`, risks) is copied into `kickoff.md`, and nothing is seeded into `plan.json`.

The risk path is manual/agent discipline: `templates/plan.template.json:48` `"source": "&lt;where the risk came from: an explorer id, runlog, or the spec node&gt;"`; `crew/planner.md:22` "A risk drawn from the run log carries `source: runlog` and reproduces exactly a heading of `flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md`"; `validate-plan.mjs:289-301` warns (never errors) when such a risk names a non-existent heading. Run 2 did carry one: `plan.json.risks[0] = { text: "run 1 was abandoned at verify because two locked cases asserted wrong values; tests-map v2 corrects them", reaction: "watch", source: "runlog" }` — note `source` is the bare word `runlog`, so the heading check finds nothing to compare and stays silent. The `watch` field of run 1's entry is never mechanically checked against run 2's evidence.

The manual's one-change rule, `endings.md:46-50`: "A retry is a new experiment against an improved setup: `fc launch new` again, fresh session, frozen spec." — "One change per retry where possible; where several fixes were forced, the run-log `watch` line names which one the retry tests and the others ride along unattributed." — "Same spec commit, same kickoff parts except the bumped one, same crew except the changed file, so the difference between runs is the change." — "When the change is to the spec, it is amended and re-frozen at a new commit, and the new launch pins the new commit; the previous launch is named in `launch.json.previous_launch` automatically." — plus the exit rules: "Retry when the diagnosis names an axis and the change is made; demote to a single session when `plan.json` held no parallel wave of two or more units …; shelve when the same axis has failed three runs straight." Checklist `endings.md:87`: "exactly one under test (`watch` says which)". None of this is enforced by any command.

## 8. THE REPORT ON ABANDON

**Assembled identically.** `fc launch end` calls the same `renderThrough(report.mjs)` for every outcome (`launch.mjs:841-846`), and `report.mjs` branches on outcome nowhere — `HEADINGS` (`report.mjs:13-21`) is a fixed list of seven headings ("The eight headings of spec I12"; the eighth is the header block). Diffing the two files: both start `# Run report · flightcrew-v1 · &lt;L&gt;`, both carry the same header lines (`spec/kickoff`, `started/ended/outcome`, `cost`, `agents/phases`) and the same section set — `## Ledger`, `## Verification`, `## Review`, `## Phases`, `## Agents`, `## Failures and interventions`, `## Orchestrator notes`. The only differences are content: the abandoned report's outcome line reads `outcome: abandoned`, its Verification section reads `checks: 27 pass · 2 fail · 0 error`, its `## Review` section reads `not run` (the `NOT_RUN` placeholder, `report.mjs:26`), and its Failures table carries the `wrong-check` escalation verbatim. Optional header lines appear only when the data exists: `landed:` (`report.mjs:97-99`) and `accepted units: … abandoned units:` (`report.mjs:100-103`) — both absent from both files.

**No verdict in its own voice.** Outcome is echoed as a data field only (`report.mjs:92`: `outcome: ${dash(launch.outcome)}`); every heading carries a provenance mark `[checked]`, `[reviewed]`, `[recorded]`, `[stated]`. `journey.md` G3 row: "the outcome then given to `fc launch end` is the decision, and `report.md` records it rather than feeding it". `run-report.md` anti-pattern: "The verdict in the report's own voice: 'ready to merge'; the reader must re-verify everything to trust the sentence." (Countervailing recorded fact: critic finding **F9** in `RUNLOG.md:14` — "report.md prints notes.md verbatim under Orchestrator notes, so a note recorded with fc launch note can carry the strings B18 forbids ('ready to merge', 'should be accepted', 'accept this run') into report.md outside quoted check output.")

## 9. GATE 3

**What it is** (`journey.md` gates table): "G3 | after `fc launch phase report`, before `fc launch end` | on the evidence page: the ledger first, then open findings, then the unverified lines (unverified behaviours, test-file changes, files outside the boundary), then the cost; orchestrator notes last | `fc launch end accepted`, `accepted-with-reservations`, `partial --units`, or `abandoned --at G3`". Approver: **human** (`journey.md:31` stage G3 row, Who = human). `endings.md:11,13` puts both accept and partial decisions "at G3". `run-log.md` line 2 of the preamble: "The gates are G1 (plan), G2 (contracts) and G3 (report)". Command: `fc launch gate G3 approve|exit` (`launch.mjs:31`).

**Why both launch.json files show G3 pending with an outcome set.** Because `fc launch end` never reads the gates. The word `G3` appears in `launch.mjs` only twice — in the help string (line 31) and in `const GATES = ['G1', 'G2', 'G3']` (line 43). In `gate()`:

```js
const source = id === 'G1' ? 'plan' : id === 'G2' ? 'contracts' : null;
const moveTo = decision === 'approve' ? (id === 'G1' ? 'contracts' : id === 'G2' ? 'implement' : null) : null;
```
(`launch.mjs:628-629`) — G3 has no source phase, no destination phase and no blocker function (only `gate2Blockers` exists, `launch.mjs:624-627`). And in `end()` the entire precondition set (`launch.mjs:786-815`, quoted in §1) contains no reference to `launchJson.gates`. So **`fc launch end` neither requires nor records G3**: it is neither a bypass nor a recording — the gate field simply stays `{"status":"pending","at":null}` while `outcome`, `status`, `ended` and `phase: "ended"` are written. Both recorded runs took exactly that path, and the schema is satisfied because `gates` requires only the three keys, not their statuses (`schemas/launch.schema.json:25-26,126-141`). `journey.md`'s own G3 row describes the human read and the outcome decision without any `fc launch gate G3` step — the gate exists as a reading ritual whose only trace is the outcome word.

## 10. HUMAN COMMAND COUNT at the ending

From "verification is green" to "ground cleared", per `journey.md:31`, `endings.md:69-75`, `launch-anatomy.md:101`:

**Accept-and-merge path:**
1. `fc launch phase report` (orchestrator per `journey.md` stage 9, human-adjacent)
2. read `evidence.html`, `fc launch status`, last critic pass — the G3 read
3. `fc launch end accepted|accepted-with-reservations|partial --units …` — fc prints `worktrees to remove: …`, `branches to delete: …`, report path
4. `git switch -c &lt;integration&gt;` / `git rebase &lt;parent&gt;` (implied by "rebase the run branch or an integration branch built from it onto the current parent"; no command given)
5. `fc verify` on the rebased branch
6. `git push`
7. open the PR with `report.md` linked (no command given; `gh pr create` is nowhere in the manuals)
8. wait for CI
9. merge the PR (squashed per unit — `endings.md:73`)
10. `fc launch land --commit &lt;sha&gt; --pr &lt;url&gt; [--evidence-commit &lt;sha&gt;]`
11. edit `flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md` — fill `kept:` and `reservation:` by hand (no command)
12. `git commit` the entry (and the setup change on the abandon path)
13. `git worktree remove &lt;path&gt;` × N — the printed lines
14. `git branch -D &lt;L&gt;/&lt;unit&gt;` × N — the printed lines
15. `git worktree prune`
16. `fc runlog show --spec &lt;S&gt;` (verify)
17. the promotion pass — no command exists (§11)

= **4 `fc` commands** (`end`, `verify`, `land`, `runlog show`), **≥5 git commands** (rebase, push, worktree remove ×N, branch -D ×N, worktree prune, commit), 1 PR action outside the tooling, 1 hand edit.

**Abandon path:** `fc launch gate &lt;G&gt; exit` (optional) → `fc launch end abandoned --at &lt;where&gt;` → hand-fill five `&lt;fill&gt;` fields → make the setup change → `git commit` (log entry + change together) → `git worktree remove` ×N → `git branch -D` ×N → `git worktree prune`. = **1–2 `fc` commands**, the rest git and editing.

## 11. PROMOTION PASS

Described in prose, in one place, with no template, command, or artefact — `run-log.md` §Promotion:

&gt; "A rule logged in two entries is promoted into a more permanent home: the constitution for a universal convention, a hook or `fc` refusal for a rule that must fire every time, the spec template or the kickoff library for a structural gap, a crew definition for a role's conduct."
&gt; "Once promoted, it stops being logged; the `promote:` line marks the candidate, and the promoting entry records `promote: &lt;rule&gt; → &lt;artefact&gt;`."
&gt; "The log stays short because its findings keep leaving it."
&gt; "Retire the same way: a promoted rule that a hook now enforces is pruned from the kickoff part that carried it."

Plus the **pattern pass** in the same manual: "Every fifth entry, the human runs a pattern pass: list the entries with `fc runlog show` and count the `fixed on` values. The axis that keeps appearing is the pillar to invest in next; three context fixes in a row means the spec template or the interview needs work, not the next spec." — the count is by eye; nothing counts axes.

References elsewhere: `endings.md:74` "promote confirmed rules"; `journey.md:31` stage title; `manuals/README.md:21` ("stage 10, and when a run-log entry's `promote:` line moves a repeated rule into a role definition") and `:49`; parallel doctrine at `spec-conventions.md:66` and `testing-conventions.md:74`/`testing-description.md:113`.

**Absent**: any command (`fc promote` does not exist), any counter of repeated rules, any checklist template, any "kickoff variants saved" mechanism. The kickoff library is a fixed set of parts under `templates/kickoff/` (`base.md`, `shape-session.md`, `shape-sessions.md`, `shape-workflow.md`, `task-agent.md`, `task-audit.md`, `task-feature.md`, `task-migration.md`); a run's rendered `kickoff.md` is written into its own launch folder and never promoted back into the library, and part versions are bumped by hand. `templates/constitution-fragment.md` exists and is printed by `fc distribute`, but nothing writes into it. The single recorded `promote:` line (`RUNLOG.md:30`) names a candidate ("C3 one-line success output versus in-process validator lines: settle in spec v2") with no mechanism behind it.

---

## Factual tensions inside the built ending

1. **`partial` is in two families at once.** `launch.mjs:42` puts `partial` in `ACCEPTED_FAMILY` (so it faces the HEAD-evidence and clean-tree gate); `runlog.mjs:23` excludes it (so it gets the abandoned-family entry). Both are deliberate and consistent with `endings.md:15` / `run-log.md:35`, but the same word names two different sets in two files.
2. **The `&lt;fill&gt;` protocol has no enforcement twin**, against `journey.md`'s binding line "Every prohibition has an enforcement twin: a hook, a permission rule or an `fc` refusal. A rule that exists only as prose is a preference." `run-log.md:60` says "An agent never writes a `&lt;fill&gt;` field"; both entries in `flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md` are prefixed `draft (orchestrator):` on every judgement field, and no command refused.
3. **G3 is a gate `fc` cannot see.** `fc launch gate G3` records a status that no command reads; `fc launch end` — the command G3 exists to authorise — checks no gate. Both runs ended with `G3: pending`.
4. **The cleanup lines are advisory strings.** `endings.md:106` calls standing worktrees and branches "the haunted repository", but the only thing standing between an abandoned run and a haunted repository is the human copying two printed lines; nothing verifies afterwards, and `fc launch new`/`activate` do not check for leftover `&lt;L&gt;/*` branches.
5. **`branches to delete:` is synthesised, not observed.** `cleanupLines` (`launch.mjs:771-772`) derives `&lt;L&gt;/&lt;unit&gt;` from `plan.json` without asking git, so it prints `git branch -D` for branches that may never have existed — as in run 1, whose report records "no unit branches were created" while every unit's Ledger row names branch `flightcrew-buildout-v1`.
6. **`fc launch land` proves evidence, not integration.** Its `integration_check` string is a restatement of `evidence/summary.json` at whatever commit the human names; it cannot tell a rebased integration branch from the pre-rebase state, and it does not require the run to have ended or been accepted. `endings.md:70` ("a unit's green from before the rebase says nothing about the rebased state") is precisely the failure mode `land` cannot detect.
7. **The retry's carry is a filename.** `kickoff.md` prints `read first: flightdeck/launch/RUNLOG.md` but the renderer never reads the file; `previous_launch` is a name; the failure reaches the next plan only if an agent chooses to write a `source: runlog` risk, and `validate-plan` then only warns about the heading text.
8. **`kept:` / `promote:` are emitted unconditionally on abandon/partial** (`runlog.mjs:110`) while `runlog-entry.template.md:21` and `run-log.md:35` call them "optional".
9. **The run-log file's own explanatory sentence has been pushed below the entries** (`RUNLOG.md:32`), a structural consequence of insert-after-first-heading.
10. **`--at` is unvalidated free text** that never lands in `launch.json`; the only record is `events.jsonl` and the derived `symptom` string. A typo'd stage is unrecoverable from the launch state.
11. **The endings guide's "three endings" and the CLI's four outcomes** are reconciled in prose (`endings.md:3`) but `launch.json.status` takes the outcome verbatim, so `status` has four terminal values and the schema's `outcome` enum, not the manual's taxonomy, is what tools see.

## Prescribed by the endings guide with no counterpart in the build

- **Integration branch / rebase / `fc verify` on the rebased state** — prose only (`endings.md:70,94`); no command creates, rebases, or verifies one, and `fc verify` has no branch argument.
- **PR opening and linking `report.md`** — prose only (`endings.md:71`); no `fc` or `gh` step in any manual command table.
- **CI running "the same gates"** — no CI configuration, workflow file, or gate-export anywhere under `flightdeck/`.
- **One squashed commit per unit, unit names matching branches matching evidence sections** (`endings.md:73`) — nothing checks the landed commit shape; `land` records one sha.
- **Wave-ordered landing to the parent** (`endings.md:69`) — `fc worker merge` orders unit→run-branch merges during the run only; nothing orders or checks the landing.
- **Deleting branches, removing worktrees, `git worktree prune`** (`endings.md:27,74,95,106`) — printed as strings, executed by nobody; `prune` is not even printed.
- **The salvage rule** (`endings.md:32-42`) — no command classifies, copies, or blocks any artefact; explorer returns and wave-0 contracts have no carry-forward mechanism into a new launch folder.
- **"Do not resume the abandoned session"** (`endings.md:29`) — no state prevents re-activating or continuing work in an ended launch beyond `activate` refusing a non-draft status.
- **"One change per retry", "same kickoff parts except the bumped one", "shelve after three runs on the same axis"** (`endings.md:46-50`) — nothing compares two launches' kickoff versions, spec commits, or `fixed on` history.
- **The human diagnosis before the next run** — no precondition on `fc launch new`, `activate`, `pin` or `phase plan` referencing RUNLOG completeness.
- **The promotion pass and the every-fifth-entry pattern pass** — no command, no counter, no template, no record that either was run.
- **The cost line "closed"** as a merge-gate condition (`endings.md:75`) — `cost` reads `not recorded` in both real entries (`RUNLOG.md:7,22`) and in both reports, and nothing refuses a landing on it; `fc launch land` never looks at cost.
- **Archiving** — `flightdeck/blackbox/archive.keep` exists; no manual sentence and no command uses it.</result>

p='endings-problems.md'; body=open(p).read()
def sect(marker, prose):
    global body
    i=body.index(marker); j=i+len(marker)
    lines=body[j:].split('\n'); k=0
    while k<len(lines) and (lines[k].startswith('<!--') or lines[k]==''):
        if lines[k]=='' and k+1<len(lines) and lines[k+1].startswith('#'): break
        k+=1
    body=body[:j]+'\n'.join(lines[:k])+'\n'+prose.strip('\n')+'\n'+'\n'.join(lines[k:])
